sections.name: Trends & Mental Health Concepts
sections.group: Unit 1: Intro to Mental Health Nursing

cards.prompt: History of mental health nursing: key eras and "firsts"
cards.promptHtml: History of mental health nursing: key eras and "firsts"
cards.answerHtml:
Moral treatment (1790–1900): Pinel, Tuke; kindness

Institutionalization (1900–1955): warehousing in state hospitals; Beers

Federal action: 1946 NIMH; 1950s chlorpromazine

Deinstitutionalization: 1963 Community Mental Health Centers Act; planned centers never materialized

Nursing: Richards (1882, first training school); Peplau 1952, first graduate program 1954

cards.prompt: Current trends in mental health nursing
cards.answerHtml:
• Evidence-based practice: first step is define the clinical question
  • Recovery-oriented, person-centered care (replaces paternalistic model)
  • Trauma-informed care; less seclusion and restraint
  • Least restrictive, community-based care (ACT, telehealth, integrated primary and behavioral care)
  • Parity laws (2008, 2010 ACA); treat co-occurring disorders together
  • Aging population, polypharmacy

cards.prompt: Mental health vs mental illness: criteria
cards.answerHtml:
Mental health: realizes abilities, copes with normal stress, works productively (WHO); 8 wellness dimensions

Mental disorder: clinically significant disturbance in thinking, emotion regulation or behavior, with distress or impaired function

Culture: judged against the person's own culture; deviance alone is not illness

  • You can have a disorder and still be well
  • Incidence = new cases; prevalence = all cases

cards.prompt: Signs of a mental health problem: what does the nurse look for?
cards.promptHtml: Signs of a mental health problem: what does the nurse look for?
cards.answerHtml:
• Appearance/behavior: disheveled, agitation or slowing
  • Mood/affect: flat, blunted, labile
  • Speech/thought: pressured, tangential; delusions, hallucinations
  • Cognition: disorientation, poor insight and judgment
  • Function: sleep, appetite, hygiene change; withdrawal

Priority: suicidal or homicidal thoughts

Older adult: somatic complaints; new confusion means rule out physical causes first

sections.name: Ethics & Standards
sections.group: Unit 1: Intro to Mental Health Nursing

cards.prompt: Standards of practice vs standards of professional performance
cards.promptHtml: Standards of practice vs standards of professional performance
cards.answerHtml:
Practice (6): assessment, diagnosis, outcomes identification, planning, implementation, evaluation

Professional performance (10): quality of practice, education, evaluation, communication, collaboration, ethics, research, resource use, leadership, environmental health

Levels: PMH-RN (ADN/BSN); PMH-APRN (master's/doctoral)

  • Prescribing and psychotherapy belong to the APRN

cards.prompt: Role of the psychiatric mental health nurse
cards.promptHtml: Role of the psychiatric mental health nurse
cards.answerHtml:
• Therapeutic use of self is the main tool
  • Assessment, safety, milieu management
  • Medication administration, monitoring, teaching
  • Case management and collaboration with the team
  • Advocacy: protect rights, person-first language, fight stigma
  • Documentation: objective, jargon-free, in pen, initial corrections
  • Baseline BMI and appetite (psych drugs cause weight gain)

cards.prompt: Ethical principles in psychiatric nursing
cards.answerHtml:
• Autonomy: patient refuses a medication
  • Beneficence/nonmaleficence: act for good; avoid needless restraint
  • Justice: equal access
  • Veracity/fidelity: tell the truth, keep promises
  • Paternalism: justified only when the person cannot deliberate

cards.prompt: Duty to warn vs confidentiality
cards.answerHtml:
• Privacy: the part of life not governed by society's laws
  • Confidentiality: duty of nondisclosure
  • Duty to warn (Tarasoff): overrides confidentiality when the patient threatens an identifiable person

Nursing: warn and protect; never promise secrecy

cards.prompt: Advance directives and capacity: what must the nurse know?
cards.promptHtml: Advance directives and capacity: what must the nurse know?
cards.answerHtml:
• Patient Self-Determination Act: Medicare/Medicaid facilities ask about advance directives on admission (not job discrimination; that is the ADA)
  • Psychiatric advance directive: made while competent
  • Competency: communicates a choice, understands, appreciates consequences, reasons about risks and benefits
  • Informed consent: benefits, costs, results of refusal

cards.prompt: Liability and forensic terms in psychiatric care
cards.promptHtml: Liability and forensic terms in psychiatric care
cards.answerHtml:
Liability: assault, battery, false imprisonment, negligence; most suits involve suicidal or violent patients

  • Holding a voluntary patient who asks to leave, with no legal basis, is false imprisonment

Forensic:

  • NGRI: secure hospital
  • GBMI: prison plus treatment
  • Unfit defendant: treat to restore fitness to stand trial

sections.name: Legal Holds & Rights
sections.group: Unit 1: Intro to Mental Health Nursing

cards.prompt: California 5150 hold
cards.answerHtml:
Length: 72 hours

Criteria: danger to self or others, or gravely disabled (cannot provide own food, clothing, shelter)

Who: peace officer or county-designated professional

Exam tip: refusing medication alone is not grounds for involuntary commitment

cards.prompt: California 5250, 5260, 5270 holds and conservatorship
cards.answerHtml:
• 5250: 14 days; certification review hearing within 4 days; writ of habeas corpus
  • 5260: +14 days for suicide attempt or threat; no hearing
  • 5270.15: +30 days if still gravely disabled
  • 5300: up to 180 days, dangerous to others; jury trial right
  • T-con: 30 days, then hearing for 1-year conservatorship

cards.prompt: Restraint and seclusion: rules and time limits
cards.promptHtml: Restraint and seclusion: rules and time limits
cards.answerHtml:
• Last resort, least restrictive first; chemical restraint counts
  • Provider order; constant observation
  • Order lasts: 4 h adults; 2 h ages 9–17; 1 h age 8 and under
  • Face-to-face evaluation within the first hour
  • Emergency: nurse may restrain first, get order within 15–30 min
  • Document every 15–30 min

cards.prompt: Patient rights: never denied vs denied only with cause
cards.promptHtml: Patient rights: never denied vs denied only with cause
cards.answerHtml:
Never denied: humane care, freedom from abuse and neglect, religion, education, nondiscrimination

Denied only with good cause (documented, reviewed, restored when cause ends): own clothing, money, visitors, phone, mail, possessions

Voluntary patients: keep full civil rights; may leave against medical advice

cards.prompt: Right to refuse medication and the Riese hearing
cards.promptHtml: Right to refuse medication and the Riese hearing
cards.answerHtml:
• Voluntary patients may refuse antipsychotics except in an emergency (immediate need to prevent serious harm, consent impractical)
  • Involuntary patients may refuse unless a capacity (Riese) hearing finds they lack capacity
  • ECT without consent needs a court finding of incapacity
  • A conservator may be given consent authority

sections.name: Role, Culture & Settings
sections.group: Unit 1: Intro to Mental Health Nursing

cards.prompt: Culture, stigma and mental illness
cards.answerHtml:
• Culture is broader than race (age, gender, religion, income, education)
  • DSM-5: cultural syndrome (ataque de nervios), idiom of distress (susto, nervios), cultural explanation
  • Stigma types: public, self, label avoidance; use person-first language
  • Implicit bias is unconscious; tools: introspection, cultural humility

Nursing: accept the idiom; do not label it a delusion

cards.prompt: Settings for mental health treatment: the continuum of care
cards.promptHtml: Settings for mental health treatment: the continuum of care
cards.answerHtml:
• Crisis intervention: under 6 h
  • 23-hour observation
  • Crisis stabilization: under 7 days
  • Acute inpatient: most restrictive; danger to self/others or unable to meet basic needs
  • Partial hospitalization: day program, no overnight stay
  • Intensive outpatient, residential, in-home, outpatient, ACT

Principle: least restrictive environment (Olmstead); discharge planning starts at admission

cards.prompt: Ongoing psychiatric assessment: the two parts of the exam
cards.promptHtml: Ongoing psychiatric assessment: the two parts of the exam
cards.answerHtml:
Part 1, history: current condition, prior diagnoses and treatment, family history

Part 2, mental status exam (MSE): present state; judges diagnosis, treatment and immediate risk of harm

  • Assessment starts at first contact and never ends
  • Repeat the MSE to see if interventions work
  • Get the client's permission before using family or records

Priority: safety

cards.prompt: Suicide screening (C-SSRS): what does the nurse do?
cards.promptHtml: Suicide screening (C-SSRS): what does the nurse do?
cards.answerHtml:
Ask: wish to be dead, thoughts of killing self, action or preparation

If yes to plan, intent or behavior:

  • do not leave the patient alone
  • notify the supervisor
  • refer to a clinician for full assessment
  • document

Done at every assessment, with assaultive thoughts

cards.prompt: Applying assessment elements: what is checked and when?
cards.promptHtml: Applying assessment elements: what is checked and when?
cards.answerHtml:
• Physical/neuro: baseline before drugs; vitals, orthostatic BP, AIMS
  • Labs: liver, kidney, WBC, electrolytes, thyroid
  • Function/nutrition: sleep, appetite, self-care, baseline BMI
  • Medications: prescribed, OTC, herbal
  • Social: family, culture, legal status, spirituality

When: admission, every shift or contact, any change

Quality assurance: accurate documentation feeds QI

cards.prompt: Psychological testing: objective vs projective vs cognitive
cards.promptHtml: Psychological testing: objective vs projective vs cognitive
cards.answerHtml:
Objective: MMPI-2, State-Trait Anxiety Inventory, Millon, Beck Depression Inventory

Projective: Rorschach, TAT, sentence completion

Cognitive: WAIS-IV, Raven's, Benton

  • Tests support the interview; they do not replace it
  • Functional status: Index of Independence in ADLs (older adults living alone)

cards.prompt: Elements of the mental status exam
cards.answerHtml:
• Appearance/behavior/attitude
  • Speech: loudness, flow, coherence
  • Emotional state: mood and affect
  • Thought content: delusions, hallucinations, obsessions, phobias
  • Orientation: time, place, person
  • Memory and attention
  • Intellectual level: reasoning, judgment
  • Insight

Exam tip: loss of orientation shows extent of confusion

cards.prompt: Mood vs affect
cards.answerHtml:
Mood: sustained emotion (euthymic, euphoric, labile, dysphoric)

Affect: observed expression; range, intensity, appropriateness

  • Full, restricted, blunted, flat
  • Compare with the cultural norm
  • Document in plain, objective language

cards.prompt: MSE bedside tests: attention, memory, abstraction, insight, judgment
cards.promptHtml: MSE bedside tests: attention, memory, abstraction, insight, judgment
cards.answerHtml:
• Attention: serial 7s from 100 (3s from 20 is easier); spell "world" backward
  • Recall: three unrelated words at 5 and 15 min
  • Abstraction: proverbs
  • Insight: awareness of own illness
  • Judgment: ability to reach a logical decision

cards.prompt: Mini-Mental State Exam (Folstein)
cards.answerHtml:
• Orientation, registration (3 words), naming, reading
  • Maximum score 30; about 10 min
  • 24–30 normal; 18–23 mild (Psych Notes: mild to moderate); 0–17 severe
  • Client must see and write
  • Used when time is limited and for organic syndromes

cards.prompt: Geriatric cognitive and depression screening tools
cards.answerHtml:
• Geriatric Depression Scale: yes/no, 15 items short form
  • Cornell Scale: depression in dementia
  • Clock drawing: sensitive early dementia screen
  • SLUMS, RAID, NPI-NH

Nursing: check hearing and vision first; reassess because orientation can change visit to visit

cards.prompt: DSM multiaxial system: the five axes
cards.answerHtml:
I: clinical disorders

II: personality disorders, intellectual disability

III: general medical conditions

IV: psychosocial and environmental problems

V: GAF

  • Axis I brings the client to therapy; Axis II keeps the client in therapy
  • Dual diagnosis = mental disorder plus addiction

cards.prompt: DSM-5-TR today: what happened to the axes and GAF?
cards.promptHtml: DSM-5-TR today: what happened to the axes and GAF?
cards.answerHtml:
• DSM-5 (2013) and DSM-5-TR (2022) dropped the axes and the GAF (verify)
  • Diagnoses are listed together; psychosocial factors use Z codes (verify)
  • Disability measured by WHODAS 2.0

Exam tip: expect the axes on a syllabus-based exam, not in current charts
cards.label: verify

cards.prompt: GAF scale in the nursing care plan
cards.promptHtml: GAF scale in the nursing care plan
cards.answerHtml:
0–100; lower score means greater impairment

  • 91–100 superior; 71–90 minimal symptoms; 51–60 moderate; 41–50 serious (suicidal ideation); 21–40 impaired reality testing; 1–20 danger to self or others

Use: plan treatment, nursing diagnosis, predict outcomes, set goals, measure response

Low score: risk for suicide/violence, self-care deficit

cards.prompt: Therapeutic vs social nurse-patient relationship
cards.answerHtml:
Therapeutic: focus only on the patient, definite purpose, goal-directed; conversation is the treatment

Social: reciprocal, meets the nurse's needs

  • Goals: trust, insight, information through active listening
  • Therapeutic use of self: intentional use of personality and knowledge
  • Rapport = harmony through warmth; empathy is not sympathy

Exam tip: a response that serves the nurse is wrong

cards.prompt: Phases of the nurse-patient relationship
cards.answerHtml:
Pre-interaction (course lecture)

Orientation: trust, purpose, boundaries, confidentiality; termination date stated early

Working: explore problems, test new behavior; transference and countertransference

Termination: independence, community resources

  • Testing behaviors (lateness, anger) are normal; stay consistent
  • Boyd uses 3 phases: orientation, working, resolution

cards.prompt: Active vs passive listening
cards.answerHtml:
Active: focused attention to verbal and nonverbal content; open-ended statements, reflection, questions

Passive: sitting quietly while the patient rambles; does not build the relationship

  • Active listening is among the first interventions
  • Silence is about 75% of the process but can feel like rejection

cards.prompt: Restating vs reflection vs validation (course tool)
cards.answerHtml:
Restating: repeats content ("You can't take it anymore")

Reflection: repeats or paraphrases the patient's words/feeling ("It sounds like you've been feeling very alone")

Validation: feelings make sense given their experience ("Given everything you've been through, it makes sense you feel overwhelmed")

Exam tip: sources define these differently; match the example

cards.prompt: General lead, broad opening, open-ended question, offering self
cards.promptHtml: General lead, broad opening, open-ended question, offering self
cards.answerHtml:
• General lead: "Go on." "Tell me more."
  • Broad opening: "Where would you like to start today?"
  • Open-ended question: "What has today been like for you?"
  • Offering self: "I'd like to sit with you for a few minutes." (shares time, not personal facts)

cards.prompt: Encouraging description, placing event in time, encouraging comparison, summarizing, acknowledging
cards.promptHtml: Encouraging description, placing event in time, encouraging comparison, summarizing, acknowledging
cards.answerHtml:
• Encouraging description: "What are the voices saying?"
  • Placing event in time: "What happened right before?" (finds triggers)
  • Encouraging comparison: "Have you felt this way before? What helped?"
  • Summarizing: condenses key points; closure
  • Acknowledging: "It took courage to share that."

cards.prompt: Clarification, focusing, observation, silence
cards.answerHtml:
• Clarification: use when meaning is unclear ("Are you saying...?")
  • Focusing: returns to one topic
  • Observation: "You are trembling."
  • Silence: time to organize thoughts; wait 5–10 s

Exam tip: eliminate closed, advice, reassurance and "why" options first; reflection when feeling is clear, clarification when meaning is unclear

cards.prompt: Responding to hallucinations and delusions (course tool)
cards.answerHtml:
Hallucinations: do not deny or confirm. "I don't hear what you're hearing, but I can see it's distressing." Ask what the voices say and whether they command anything

Delusions: do not agree, do not argue; acknowledge the feeling ("It sounds like you feel very unsafe")

cards.prompt: Responding to suicidal ideation, anger, crying and refusal to talk
cards.promptHtml: Responding to suicidal ideation, anger, crying and refusal to talk
cards.answerHtml:
• Suicidal ideation: stay calm, ask directly (does not plant the idea); ask plan and means; notify the instructor and patient's nurse immediately
  • Anger: lower voice, slow pace, use name, give space, never block the exit
  • Crying: offer tissue; do not rush it
  • Refusal to talk: respect it; offer presence

cards.prompt: Nontherapeutic: advice, false reassurance, clichés, minimizing
cards.answerHtml:
• Advice: "You should..."; implies nurse knows best, fosters dependency
  • False reassurance: "Everything will be fine"; may be untrue, stops exploration
  • Cliché: "I know exactly how you feel"; breaks trust
  • Minimizing: "At least you have your family"; invalidates

cards.prompt: Nontherapeutic: "why" and closed-ended questions, probing
cards.answerHtml:
• "Why" questions: sound accusing; patient often does not know
  • Closed-ended questions: yes/no, stop sharing (course tool lists as nontherapeutic; ATI allows sparingly for specific data)
  • Probing/interrogating: invasive, defensive

Fix: use open-ended statements

cards.prompt: Nontherapeutic: agreeing or challenging delusions, defending, interpreting
cards.promptHtml: Nontherapeutic: agreeing or challenging delusions, defending, interpreting
cards.answerHtml:
• Agreeing with a delusion: reinforces it
  • Challenging a delusion: "That's not real"; increases distrust and distress
  • Defending others: "Your doctor is doing her best"; dismisses the complaint
  • Interpreting/analyzing: nurse decides what it means

Better: respond to the feeling

cards.prompt: Nontherapeutic: changing subject, personal opinions, approval/disapproval
cards.answerHtml:
• Changing the topic: nurse's anxiety takes over; topic feels off-limits
  • Personal opinions/self-disclosure: shifts focus to the nurse
  • Approval/agreement: patient cannot reconsider the view
  • Disapproval: belittles; patient avoids the nurse
  • Promising secrecy: cannot be kept when safety is involved

cards.prompt: Verbal vs nonverbal communication
cards.answerHtml:
• Verbal = words, emotion and context; nonverbal = gestures, posture, eye contact, expression
  • When they conflict, rely on the nonverbal ("I feel fine" while slumped)
  • Nurse: eye level, uncrossed arms, lean slightly forward
  • Paralanguage = voice use; kinesics = body motion
  • Zones: intimate 0–18 in; personal 18–40 in; social 4–12 ft; public over 12 ft

cards.prompt: Culture and communication barriers
cards.answerHtml:
• Eye contact, touch and personal space vary by culture
  • A behavior is significant only if it differs from that patient's norm
  • Ask permission before entering personal space
  • Use a trained interpreter who is not a family member
  • Cultural brokering bridges patient and system

Exam tip: patient avoids eye contact? Assess what it means first; do not label it depression

cards.prompt: Confrontation: how to use it
cards.answerHtml:
• Points out the discrepancy between what the patient says and does ("You say you want to stay out of the hospital, but you stop your medications")
  • Timing is crucial; use cautiously, after trust
  • Nonjudgmental tone
  • Can alienate the patient if misused

cards.prompt: Self-disclosure, immediacy and role playing
cards.answerHtml:
• Self-disclosure: generally avoid; disclose only with a therapeutic purpose, then return to the patient
  • Immediacy: addressing what is happening between nurse and patient right now (verify)
  • Role playing: rehearse a hard situation; discuss feelings before and after; patient tries it in real life
cards.label: verify

cards.prompt: Boundaries: when are they needed and what are warning signs?
cards.promptHtml: Boundaries: when are they needed and what are warning signs?
cards.answerHtml:
Needed: vulnerable patients, power imbalance, focus on patient needs

Warning signs:

  • gift giving
  • extra time with one patient
  • defending the patient strongly
  • feeling you alone understand
  • keeping secrets

Action: seek supervision or transfer care; tell the team

At termination: no phone number, no meeting outside

cards.prompt: Transference vs countertransference
cards.answerHtml:
Transference: patient assigns feelings about an important figure to the nurse (e.g., a former authority figure)

Countertransference: nurse's emotional reaction from own needs and conflicts (overidentifying, competing, arguing)

  • Both occur in the working phase

Nursing: recognize it; use supervision

cards.prompt: Self-awareness and process recording
cards.answerHtml:
• Self-awareness: knowing your beliefs, biases and limits; required for a therapeutic relationship
  • Ongoing self-examination with a trusted person
  • Process recording: verbatim record from memory, with nonverbal behavior, analyzed for blocks and themes
  • Journal after hard conversations

Strong feelings about a patient: self-examine and seek supervision; do not withdraw care

cards.prompt: Basic principles of group work: open vs closed, size, seating
cards.promptHtml: Basic principles of group work: open vs closed, size, seating
cards.answerHtml:
• Open: members come and go (inpatient)
  • Closed: same members (outpatient psychotherapy)
  • Small (7–8 or fewer): cohesive; large: education, more conflict
  • Seating: circle, no table
  • First meeting: purpose, rules, times, confidentiality
  • Dynamics = interactions; process = movement toward goals

cards.prompt: Hidden agenda vs group norm vs groupthink
cards.promptHtml: Hidden agenda vs group norm vs groupthink
cards.answerHtml:
Hidden agenda: covert goals that disrupt the group

Group norm: behavior that gives structure (raising hands)

Groupthink: avoiding conflict and adopting the leader's view

Cohesiveness: ability to stick together

Homogeneous: shared diagnosis or gender

cards.prompt: Types of therapeutic groups
cards.answerHtml:
• Psychoeducation: time-limited lesson
  • Support: nurse-led
  • Psychotherapy: master's-prepared leader
  • Self-help: AA, no professional leader
  • Task / decision-making
  • Medication group: open, weekly, small

Acute setting: members change daily, focus on relief

cards.prompt: Phases of group development and the leader's job
cards.promptHtml: Phases of group development and the leader's job
cards.answerHtml:
Beginning (forming): polite, anxious, testing; leader is active, sets tone and confidentiality

Middle, conflict (storming): power struggles, scapegoating; leader stays neutral

Middle, working (norming): cohesion, real sharing

End (performing/termination): grief; summarize gains

  • Conflict is normal; do not end the group

cards.prompt: Leader responses by group phase
cards.answerHtml:
• Unsure members: be active, give structure, limit monopolizing
  • Members test the leader: let them "pass," stay open
  • Increasing self-disclosure: encourage problem solving
  • Separation feelings: set the termination date in advance, explore supports
  • Self-reflective loop: what happened, here and now, why

cards.prompt: Group member roles: task, maintenance, individual
cards.answerHtml:
Task: keep to purpose (recorder, coordinator, information seeker)

Maintenance: keep the group together (harmonizer, encourager, compromiser)

Individual: meet personal needs, hurt teamwork (dominator, aggressor, recognition seeker, blocker)

Exam tip: mediates and relieves tension = harmonizer

cards.prompt: Challenging group members: monopolizer, "yes, but," silent, disliked
cards.promptHtml: Challenging group members: monopolizer, "yes, but," silent, disliked
cards.answerHtml:
• Monopolizer: acknowledge, redirect to others, limit time
  • "Yes, but...": do not problem-solve for them; model problem solving
  • Silent member: respect silence; understand it first
  • Disliked member: stay neutral, show respect
  • Conflict: leader-member conflict needs care (power difference)

cards.prompt: Yalom's therapeutic factors in groups
cards.answerHtml:
Hope, universality, imparting information, altruism, corrective recapitulation of family, socializing techniques, imitative behavior, interpersonal learning, cohesiveness, catharsis, existential factors

Examples:

  • "I'm not the only one with voices" = universality
  • copying the leader's anger handling = imitative behavior
  • supporting a new member = altruism

cards.prompt: Facilitating techniques used by the group leader
cards.promptHtml: Facilitating techniques used by the group leader
cards.answerHtml:
• Support, summarizing, clarification, reflecting feelings/behavior
  • Confrontation: names disruptive behavior (needs support)
  • Probing: experienced leaders
  • Leader stays neutral, no favorites, does not reveal own beliefs
  • Start and end on time; co-leader observes and records

cards.prompt: Cognitive behavioral therapy: principles
cards.answerHtml:
• Structured method to replace distorted thoughts and change behavior rewards
  • Core idea: people are disturbed by their perception of events
  • Triangle: trigger, thought, feeling, behavior
  • Cognitive triad: negative view of self, world, future
  • Distortions: overgeneralization, personalizing, catastrophizing, selective abstraction
  • Schema: early life rules

cards.prompt: CBT treatment components
cards.answerHtml:
• Collaborative relationship, strengths emphasized
  • Assessment, goals, contract for 10–12 sessions
  • Agenda each session; homework (thought records, journaling)
  • Test beliefs: evidence for and against
  • Termination: prepare for setbacks, booster sessions

Goal: patient becomes independent

Exam tip: test the belief; do not say "that's silly"

cards.prompt: REBT and solution-focused brief therapy
cards.answerHtml:
REBT (Ellis), ABCDE: Activating event, Beliefs, Consequences, Dispute, Effective outlook

SFBT: solutions and strengths, small goals

  • miracle, exception, scaling, relationship questions; compliments
  • fits short inpatient stays and 15-minute home visits

cards.prompt: How CBT is used in treatment, and its limits
cards.promptHtml: How CBT is used in treatment, and its limits
cards.answerHtml:
Inpatient: SFBT, journaling, medication homework

Primary care: insomnia, depression, chronic pain, anxiety

Community/home: small, concrete goals

Useful for: substance abuse with psychiatric symptoms

Limits: rigid use neglects the relationship; poor fit for thought disorders

Fearful or severely dysfunctional: behavioral techniques first

cards.prompt: Systematic desensitization, flooding and response prevention
cards.answerHtml:
• Systematic desensitization: gradual exposure paired with relaxation; patient masters relaxation first; phobias
  • Flooding: large amount of the stimulus at once, therapist present
  • Response prevention: block the compulsion until anxiety falls (OCD)

cards.prompt: Modeling, operant conditioning, aversion therapy, thought stopping
cards.promptHtml: Modeling, operant conditioning, aversion therapy, thought stopping
cards.answerHtml:
• Modeling: demonstrate behavior to copy
  • Operant conditioning: reward the target behavior (tokens)
  • Aversion therapy: pair unwanted behavior with an unpleasant stimulus; needs supervision
  • Thought stopping: say "stop," substitute a positive thought

cards.prompt: DBT and other psychotherapies
cards.answerHtml:
• DBT: mindfulness, distress tolerance; borderline personality disorder with self-harm
  • Psychoanalysis: free association, dream analysis, transference
  • Psychodynamic: focus on the present
  • IPT: relationships, bereavement
  • Family therapy: generalist nurse does counseling, education, genograms

cards.prompt: How are psychotropic drugs used in mental health care?
cards.promptHtml: How are psychotropic drugs used in mental health care?
cards.answerHtml:
Principle: match the drug to target symptoms (specific, measurable)

  • anything else it does is a side effect; a serious physiologic one is an adverse reaction
  • classes cross diagnoses (antidepressants for anxiety/OCD; antipsychotics for mania)
  • partial response: augmentation or combinations

Plan: one arm of care with psychotherapy, ECT, light therapy, psychoeducation

Reference: the Prescribing Information and any boxed warning

cards.prompt: Phases of drug treatment
cards.answerHtml:
Initiation: treat the first dose as a test dose

Stabilization: titration; therapeutic drug monitoring matters most here

Maintenance: prevent relapse, teach self-monitoring

Discontinuation: taper

Timelines: antidepressants ~2 weeks to work, continue 6-12 months after remission; antipsychotics 1-2 weeks for change, 6-12 week trials

cards.prompt: FDA drug trial phases
cards.answerHtml:
• Phase I: dose range in healthy people
  • Phase II: effective dose in a limited group with the disorder
  • Phase III: large multisite trials, ends in a new drug application
  • Phase IV: post-marketing surveillance for rare reactions

Note: a drug is approved only for the indications tested

cards.prompt: Patient says "I feel better, so I'll stop my medication"
cards.promptHtml: Patient says "I feel better, so I'll stop my medication"
cards.answerHtml:
Teach:

  • stopping abruptly risks relapse or discontinuation symptoms
  • do not stop on your own; call the prescriber

Nursing:

  • explore the reason first; reasons to stop differ from reasons to refuse
  • the drug is one part of a plan, not the whole treatment

cards.prompt: Neurotransmitters: function and disorder link
cards.answerHtml:
• Dopamine: movement, reward, psychosis/mood
  • Norepinephrine: arousal, fight or flight; mood/anxiety
  • Serotonin: mood, sleep, appetite; depressed mood/psychosis
  • Acetylcholine: learning, memory; cognition
  • GABA: main inhibitory; anxiety
  • Glutamate: main excitatory; Huntington/psychosis

cards.prompt: How do psychotropic drugs alter brain function?
cards.promptHtml: How do psychotropic drugs alter brain function?
cards.answerHtml:
Four targets: receptors, ion channels, enzymes, carrier proteins

  • Agonists mimic the transmitter; antagonists block it
  • reuptake inhibitors block carrier proteins
  • MAOIs inhibit the enzyme that breaks down monoamines
  • benzodiazepines enhance GABA at the GABA-chloride channel

cards.prompt: Side effects follow the receptor pathway
cards.answerHtml:
• D2 block, basal ganglia: EPS (acetylcholine excess with dopamine blockade, so anticholinergics treat it)
  • D2 block, tuberoinfundibular: high prolactin
  • Muscarinic block: dry mouth, constipation, urinary retention
  • Histamine block: sedation, weight gain
  • Alpha-1 block: orthostasis

Exam tip: "why this side effect" = name the receptor system

cards.prompt: Pharmacokinetics for the nurse
cards.answerHtml:
Steps: absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion

  • liver CYP450: inhibitors raise levels, inducers lower them; smoking induces CYP1A2
  • lithium and gabapentin are cleared by the kidney (monitor renal function)
  • ~4 half-lives clear >90% of a drug; steady state ~4-5 half-lives (verify)

Exam tip: "what do I monitor" = the organ that clears the drug
cards.label: verify

cards.prompt: Genetics, pharmacogenomics and culture in drug response
cards.promptHtml: Genetics, pharmacogenomics and culture in drug response
cards.answerHtml:
• no single gene causes a major disorder; several genes plus environment raise risk
  • CYP2D6 / CYP2C19: poor metabolizers get more adverse reactions; rapid metabolizers get levels too low
  • testing helps with a personal/family history of adverse reactions
  • testing refines drug choice and dose; it does not diagnose
  • Ethnopsychopharmacology: some groups need lower doses (Asian patients often one-half to one-third the antipsychotic dose)

cards.prompt: Brain structures and neuroplasticity
cards.answerHtml:
• Frontal lobes: executive function, judgment
  • Limbic system (amygdala, hippocampus, hypothalamus): emotion and memory
  • Basal ganglia: movement
  • Neuroplasticity: the brain can reorganize and restore function; supports recovery-oriented care
  • Gut-brain axis / psychoneuroimmunology: link stress, HPA axis, immunity

cards.prompt: Nursing role in psychopharmacology
cards.answerHtml:
Before: baseline allergies, meds, supplements, pregnancy, substance use, vitals, labs; document target symptoms

Give: observe the first dose

Teach: name, action, dose, side effects, what to report

Monitor: drug levels; coordinate with prescriber

Home: written plan with emergency numbers; home-health draws for clozapine; pill organizers (verify)
cards.label: verify

cards.prompt: Common side effects: nursing management
cards.answerHtml:
• Dry mouth: sugarless candy, rinse
  • Constipation: fiber, fluids
  • Orthostasis: rise slowly, dangle legs
  • Photosensitivity: sunscreen
  • Resting pulse >120: withhold and notify

Priority: assess and act on distressing side effects right away; unaddressed ones drive nonadherence

cards.prompt: Medication adherence
cards.answerHtml:
Looks like: full, partial or nil; partial is most common; about half or more with schizophrenia do not take antipsychotics as prescribed

Top reason: side effects

Nursing:

  • support the patient's decision, no coercion
  • psychoeducation, family involvement
  • long-acting injectables when adherence risk is high

cards.prompt: Polypharmacy and incompatibilities
cards.answerHtml:
Polypharmacy: several drugs from a class or many drugs overall; raises interaction and adverse-effect risk; know the rationale for each drug

Incompatible pairs:

  • MAOI plus serotonergic drugs (serotonin syndrome)
  • lithium plus NSAIDs, ACE inhibitors, thiazides (raises lithium level)
  • St. John's wort plus antidepressants (serotonin syndrome)

cards.prompt: Nutrition points with psychotropic drugs
cards.answerHtml:
• Weight gain/metabolic: second-generation antipsychotics, mirtazapine, lithium; diet and exercise teaching
  • Lithium: steady sodium, 6-8 glasses water/day; dehydration raises levels
  • Constipation: anticholinergics; fiber and fluids
  • Grapefruit juice: interacts with some drugs
  • MAOIs: tyramine-free diet
  • Lurasidone, ziprasidone: take with food (~350 calories)

cards.prompt: Geriatric considerations: psychotropic drugs
cards.answerHtml:
Why: slower gastric emptying, lower albumin (more free drug), reduced liver and kidney clearance, more anticholinergic sensitivity

Rule: start low, go slow

Avoid:

  • benzodiazepines (short term, with caution; fall risk)
  • anticholinergics in dementia
  • antipsychotics: boxed warning for dementia-related psychosis

Exam tip: new confusion after a new drug = drug reaction until proven otherwise

cards.prompt: Right to refuse medication; drug advertising
cards.answerHtml:
Right to refuse: a competent patient may refuse; involuntary medication only in an emergency or by legal process

Advertising: can create unrealistic expectations; teach from the Prescribing Information

cards.prompt: Schizophrenia: definition and diagnostic criteria
cards.answerHtml:
Is: chronic, severe disorder of thought, perception, emotion, behavior; key factor is psychosis

Criteria:

  • 2 or more: delusions, hallucinations, disorganized speech, disorganized/catatonic behavior, negative symptoms
  • at least one must be delusions, hallucinations or disorganized speech
  • active symptoms about 1 month; continuous signs 6 months or more
  • function below prior level; mood disorder, substances, medical causes ruled out

cards.prompt: Positive vs negative symptoms
cards.answerHtml:
Positive (excess or distortion): hallucinations, delusions, disorganized speech and behavior

Negative (loss of function): flat affect, alogia, avolition, anhedonia

  • negative symptoms block self-care, work, relationships
  • negative symptoms may appear first but are harder to spot

Drugs: first-generation mainly treat positive symptoms; second-generation treat both

cards.prompt: Hallucination vs delusion vs illusion
cards.answerHtml:
Hallucination: a sense with no stimulus (auditory most common)

Delusion: fixed false belief, not changed by reasoning (persecutory, grandiose, somatic, nihilistic)

Illusion: misreading a real stimulus

Command hallucination: voices tell the patient to act; ask what they say, assess harm to self or others

cards.prompt: Disorganized thinking: terms to recognize
cards.answerHtml:
• Loose associations: shifts with no link
  • Tangentiality: detours and never returns
  • Circumstantiality: long detail, eventually reaches the point (verify)
  • Word salad: unconnected words
  • Neologism: made-up word
  • Clang: words chosen by sound
  • Echolalia / echopraxia: copies words / movements
cards.label: verify

cards.prompt: Schizophrenia theories
cards.answerHtml:
Biologic: dopamine (D2 overactivity = positive symptoms; low prefrontal dopamine, hypofrontality = cognitive deficits); glutamate/GABA (PCP mimics psychosis); larger ventricles, smaller brain volume; neurodevelopmental insult

Psychosocial: stress-vulnerability model; trauma, urban living, cannabis, stigma

Genetic: first-degree relatives have 10 times the risk

cards.prompt: Prodromal period vs acute illness
cards.answerHtml:
Prodrome: tension, poor sleep, poor concentration, loss of interest, social withdrawal, new religious preoccupation, sometimes voices

Acute: behavior too bizarre or disruptive to ignore; self-care fails; high suicide risk

Nursing: screen and refer early; do not wait for hallucinations

cards.prompt: Schizophrenia spectrum: duration ladder
cards.answerHtml:
• Brief psychotic: 1 day to under 1 month; sudden onset
  • Schizophreniform: 1 to 6 months; about 1/3 recover, 2/3 progress to schizophrenia
  • Schizophrenia: 6 months or more
  • Schizoaffective: psychosis plus a mood episode; better outcome
  • Delusional disorder: stable delusions, function preserved
  • Substance-induced: lasts as long as the substance (withdrawal effects can last weeks)

cards.prompt: Older schizophrenia subtypes (DSM-IV, five types)
cards.answerHtml:
DSM-5 and DSM-5-TR dropped subtypes, but the syllabus lists them.

  • Paranoid: persecutory/grandiose delusions, voices; best prognosis (verify)
  • Disorganized: disorganized speech and behavior, flat or silly affect; worst prognosis (verify)
  • Catatonic: stupor, mutism, posturing, waxy flexibility; watch fluids, skin, injury
  • Undifferentiated: fits no single type
  • Residual: past episode, now negative symptoms
cards.label: verify

cards.prompt: Phases of schizophrenia: focus of care
cards.answerHtml:
Acute: safety and symptom relief; start medication, low stimulation, sleep, fluids

Stabilization: medication regimen (6-12 week trial), stop substances, early rehab, teach when lucid

Recovery: relapse prevention, coping, family and community support

Relapse: stopping medication nearly always causes it

cards.prompt: Three common problems with severe mental illness
cards.promptHtml: Three common problems with severe mental illness
cards.answerHtml:
• Nonadherence and relapse: side effects, lack of insight, cost
  • Medical comorbidity and early death: obesity, diabetes, metabolic syndrome, heart and lung disease, hepatitis, HIV; leading causes are medical
  • Substance use, depression, suicide: 50% attempt, 10-15% die by suicide

Also common: poverty, homelessness, stigma

cards.prompt: Anosognosia
cards.answerHtml:
Is: lack of awareness of one's own illness

Why it matters: delays treatment, drives nonadherence

Nursing: build trust anyway; ask nonjudgmentally; do not argue the diagnosis

cards.prompt: Nursing care of hallucinations
cards.answerHtml:
Do:

  • validate the feeling ("that sounds frightening")
  • state your own perception ("I do not hear the voices")
  • say "the voices," not "they"
  • redirect to the here and now
  • ask what command voices say; assess harm to self or others

Do not: argue, say it is not real, or pretend to share it

cards.prompt: Nursing care of delusions
cards.answerHtml:
Do:

  • acknowledge the fear, say you do not share the belief ("your belief that...")
  • offer safety; link flare-ups to anxiety triggers
  • be matter-of-fact; give personal space

Do not: argue, agree, whisper or write notes out of view, or change the subject abruptly

Exam answer: "The FBI is listening" = acknowledge fear, not the belief

cards.prompt: Therapeutic relationship with a psychotic patient
cards.answerHtml:
• calm, consistent, nonjudgmental
  • short, time-limited contacts
  • keep every promise
  • low stimulation in the acute phase
  • restraint or seclusion only as a last resort, with a debrief

cards.prompt: Nursing priorities: schizophrenia
cards.answerHtml:
Order: safety, then physical care, then medication monitoring

Watch:

  • suicide and violence risk
  • self-care and routine
  • thermoregulation (clothing unsuited to weather)
  • fluid balance (polydipsia)
  • weight, lipids, glucose; AIMS baseline

cards.prompt: Polydipsia and water intoxication
cards.answerHtml:
Is: compulsive fluid drinking causing low sodium

Danger: water intoxication, a medical emergency

Nursing:

  • monitor intake, daily weight, urine specific gravity
  • one-to-one for severe cases
  • report confusion, seizures (verify)
cards.label: verify

cards.prompt: Teaching a patient with schizophrenia
cards.answerHtml:
Method (errorless learning):

  • one fact at a time, small segments
  • minimal distractions, simple visuals
  • give the correct answer, have the patient write it down; avoid guessing questions
  • repeat; teach during a lucid period

cards.prompt: Family of a patient with schizophrenia
cards.answerHtml:
Reaction: shock, denial, then overwhelm; parents often become lifelong caregivers

Teach: disease course, medications (stress consistent use), relapse signs, coping, community resources, safety

Respect: the patient defines who family is

cards.prompt: Medication adherence in schizophrenia
cards.answerHtml:
Why they stop: weight gain, sedation, akathisia, no insight, cost

Helps: simple regimen, long-acting injectables, treat side effects promptly, family involvement

Inpatient: confirm the pill is swallowed (cheeking)

Do not: scold; assess and involve the prescriber

cards.prompt: Evidence-based services for severe mental illness
cards.answerHtml:
• ACT (team, home visits): best for frequent relapse and rehospitalization
  • family psychoeducation, support groups
  • CBT, cognitive remediation, social skills training
  • supported employment (best vocational method)
  • case management; integrated primary and mental health care
  • coordinated specialty care for first episode

cards.prompt: Nutrition and weight in schizophrenia
cards.answerHtml:
Why: antipsychotics raise appetite and weight; BMI 27 or more is a diabetes risk

Baseline: weight, waist, lipids, glucose

Act: weight program at first sign of gain (about 5-10 lb over desired); food diary, small goals, affordable easy foods

cards.prompt: Geriatric schizophrenia
cards.answerHtml:
• course may improve with age but cognitive decline rises
  • start low, go slow
  • more parkinsonism, sedation, falls
  • boxed warning: increased death in dementia-related psychosis

cards.prompt: Major depressive disorder (MDD)
cards.answerHtml:
Looks like: depressed mood or loss of interest for 2 weeks or more, plus others to total 5 of 9

Mnemonic (A SAD FACES): appetite, sleep, anhedonia, dysphoria, fatigue, agitation/retardation, concentration, esteem/guilt, suicide

Never: a manic or hypomanic episode

cards.prompt: Persistent depressive disorder (dysthymia)
cards.answerHtml:
• milder depressed mood most days for 2 years or more
  • plus 2 or more: appetite change, sleep, low energy, low self-esteem, poor concentration, hopelessness
  • early onset; can progress to MDD
  • appetite often increased

cards.prompt: PMDD, DMDD and seasonal affective disorder
cards.answerHtml:
• PMDD: irritability and depression in the luteal phase, improve after menses starts
  • DMDD: onset before age 10, severe outbursts about 2-3 times a week
  • SAD: recurrent winter depression: fatigue, oversleeping, carbohydrate craving; first-line is light therapy

cards.prompt: Bipolar I vs bipolar II vs cyclothymia
cards.promptHtml: Bipolar I vs bipolar II vs cyclothymia
cards.answerHtml:
• Bipolar I: at least one manic episode (7 days or more); depression common, not required; about 50% have psychosis in mania
  • Bipolar II: hypomania (4 days or more) plus major depression; never full mania
  • Cyclothymia: hypomanic and depressive symptoms 2 years or more, never full criteria

Tip: 2 wk MDD, 2 yr dysthymia/cyclothymia, 7 d mania, 4 d hypomania

cards.prompt: Mania: signs (DIGFAST)
cards.answerHtml:
DIGFAST: Distractibility, Impulsivity, Grandiosity, Flight of ideas, Activity increase, Sleep deficit, Talkativeness

  • elevated or irritable mood; needs 3 extra symptoms (4 if only irritable)
  • poor judgment: spending, sex, risks
  • can mimic ADHD; alcohol, cocaine, caffeine can trigger it; thyroid disease and drugs can mimic it

cards.prompt: Mixed episode
cards.answerHtml:
Is: full mania and full depression criteria together for 1 week

Danger: extreme agitation, high suicide risk

Nursing: safety first, close observation

cards.prompt: Mood disorder theories
cards.answerHtml:
• Biologic: low norepinephrine, dopamine, serotonin; HPA axis, thyroid; cytokines; gut-brain axis
  • Psychodynamic: anger turned inward
  • Cognitive (Beck): negative view of self, world, future
  • Behavioral: fewer rewards, more withdrawal
  • Bipolar: highly heritable; sleep loss can trigger mania
  • women 2-3 times more likely to have depression

cards.prompt: Depression across the lifespan
cards.answerHtml:
• Youth: irritable mood, somatic and anxiety complaints
  • Older adults: highest suicide risk; somatic complaints; pseudodementia; assess dehydration and weight loss
  • screen: PHQ-9 (item 9 = death/self-harm), PHQ-9A (12-17), Geriatric Depression Scale
  • rule out thyroid, anemia, drug causes

cards.prompt: Suicide risk factors and warning signs
cards.answerHtml:
Greatest predictor: previous attempt

Risk: depression or bipolar (incl. mixed), substance use, hopelessness, impulsivity, loss, isolation, access to lethal means

Warning (IS PATH WARM): ideation, substance use, purposelessness, anxiety, trapped, hopelessness, withdrawal, anger, recklessness, mood change

Clues: giving possessions away, goodbyes, detailed plan

cards.prompt: Suicide assessment: what the nurse asks
cards.answerHtml:
Ask directly (asking does not plant the idea). Assess:

  • intent to die
  • severity of ideation
  • availability of means
  • degree of planning

Priority: thought content and self-harm come first in any assessment

cards.prompt: Depressed patient who is suddenly calm or energized
cards.promptHtml: Depressed patient who is suddenly calm or energized
cards.answerHtml:
Concern: deep depression saps the energy to act; returning energy raises risk, and sudden calm may mean the patient has decided on suicide

Nursing: do not relax precautions; ask directly about plan; notify team

Also: shame after mania can drive suicide

cards.prompt: Suicide precautions: nursing interventions
cards.answerHtml:
• precautions per policy, remove hazards, constant or close observation, limit passes
  • ask about plan and means; family removes firearms
  • talk with the patient while observing; instill hope
  • no no-suicide contract (not shown to work)

cards.prompt: Suicidality warning when treatment starts
cards.answerHtml:
Boxed warning: raised suicidal thoughts in children, adolescents and young adults (under 25), especially in the first weeks or after a dose change

Nursing: watch closely, teach family to report new agitation or suicidal talk

Overdose: older tricyclic drugs are lethal in overdose; SSRIs are least lethal

cards.prompt: Nursing care of depression
cards.answerHtml:
• calm, quiet, empathic approach
  • no cheerleading, no "why" questions
  • small steps (sit up, walk to bathroom, AM care)
  • restore sleep and nutrition first; exercise at current level
  • encourage groups

Example: "You didn't sleep well last night?"

cards.prompt: Nursing care of mania
cards.answerHtml:
• low stimulation without isolating
  • simple, direct commands; no arguing; consistent limits
  • redirect flight of ideas; walk and talk
  • portable high-calorie finger foods and fluids
  • protect from exhaustion and poor judgment

Gifts: "I'm here to provide care and cannot accept this."

cards.prompt: Bipolar disorder: treatment foundation
cards.answerHtml:
First line: a mood stabilizer (lithium, valproate, carbamazepine, lamotrigine), plus atypical antipsychotic if needed

Risk: treating bipolar depression with an antidepressant alone can switch the patient into mania or rapid cycling

Relapse clue: loss of more than 1 hour of sleep a night; keep regular sleep, meals, activity

cards.prompt: Depression treatment course
cards.answerHtml:
• mild: CBT or interpersonal therapy; severe or recurrent: combined therapy and medication
  • drug effect takes about 2 weeks; acute phase 6-12 weeks
  • continue 6-12 months after remission, then taper; never stop abruptly
  • avoid St. John wort and SAMe with antidepressants (serotonin syndrome)

cards.prompt: Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT)
cards.answerHtml:
Is: brief current causes a seizure under short-acting anesthesia and muscle relaxant; 2-3 times a week, 6-12 treatments

For: severe or resistant depression, suicidality, catatonia, malnutrition, severe mania

Avoid/high risk: raised intracranial pressure, recent MI or stroke

Side effects: headache, nausea, confusion, memory loss

cards.prompt: ECT: before, during, after
cards.answerHtml:
Before: written informed consent, NPO after midnight, ECG and labs, remove dentures/jewelry, driver arranged

During: IV, 100% oxygen, bite block, BP and ECG monitoring

After:

  • airway first, oxygen until breathing returns
  • side-lying position (verify)
  • vital signs, reorient, supervise 12 hours
cards.label: verify

cards.prompt: Light therapy and other somatic treatments
cards.answerHtml:
• Light therapy (SAD): 10,000 lux for about 30 minutes each morning (older protocol: 2,500 lux for 1-2 hours)
  • rTMS: awake, no anesthesia, 20-30 sessions over 4-6 weeks, for resistant depression
  • Vagus nerve stimulation: resistant depression
  • Esketamine nasal spray: rapid effect; given under observation; risks sedation, respiratory depression

cards.prompt: Normal grief vs depression
cards.answerHtml:
Normal grief: waves of pain with movement; self-esteem intact; function recovers

Complicated grief or MDD: stuck; yearning beyond 6 months; worthlessness, guilt; persistent impairment

Suicidal thoughts and worthlessness point to depression; screen for death wishes

Risk: sudden, violent or multiple losses

cards.prompt: Postpartum mood disorders
cards.answerHtml:
• Baby blues: peak about day 4, clear within 2 weeks, function intact
  • Postpartum depression: depressive episode after delivery; about 10-15%; screen with the EPDS
  • Postpartum psychosis: about 1-2 per 1,000; emergency; infanticide and suicide risk

cards.prompt: Stress and its role in mental health
cards.promptHtml: Stress and its role in mental health
cards.answerHtml:
Stress: process from real or perceived demands appraised as threatening or benign; physiologic, psychological, social lenses

  • Eustress positive and motivating; distress negative
  • Acute: fight-or-flight, time-limited; chronic: wear and tear, raises allostatic load
  • sustained cortisol is immunosuppressive

Diathesis-stress: genetic predisposition plus a stressor can trigger or worsen a disorder

cards.prompt: Stress theorists: match the theory
cards.answerHtml:
• Cannon: homeostasis, fight-or-flight
  • Selye: general adaptation syndrome
  • McEwen: allostasis, allostatic load
  • Lazarus and Folkman: transactional model, appraisal
  • Holmes and Rahe: life events, life-change units

cards.prompt: General adaptation syndrome and the HPA axis
cards.promptHtml: General adaptation syndrome and the HPA axis
cards.answerHtml:
GAS stages: alarm, resistance, exhaustion

HPA cascade: hypothalamus releases CRH, pituitary releases ACTH, adrenal cortex releases cortisol

Allostatic load patterns: failure to adapt, prolonged heightened response, blunted response

cards.prompt: Appraisal, personality types and support
cards.answerHtml:
Primary appraisal: threat, harm or challenge; secondary: can I cope?; then reappraisal

Type A: competitive, time-urgent; most stress-prone

Type B: relaxed

Type C: conflict-avoidant, hopelessness

Type D: distressed, pessimistic, inhibited (worse coronary and diabetes outcomes)

Support: emotional, tangible, informational; women tend toward tend-and-befriend

cards.prompt: Stress assessment and nursing care
cards.answerHtml:
Goals: resolve the situation, lower the stress response, build positive coping

Assess: current stressor, coping resources; sleep, appetite, weight, tension; substance, medication and herbal use; emotions and appraisal; social network, recent life changes

Interventions: routines, diet, exercise, relaxation, guided imagery, problem solving; refer for biofeedback or hypnosis if severe

Tip: chronic stress is easy to miss; ask directly

cards.prompt: Anxiety: normal vs disorder
cards.answerHtml:
Anxiety: uncomfortable apprehension or dread with physical, emotional, cognitive, behavioral symptoms

Normal: realistic in intensity and duration, motivates action, relief follows; 3 parts: physiologic arousal, cognitive processes, coping

Disorder: out of proportion to the situation

Role in stress: stress is the demand; anxiety is a common response to perceived threat

Biology: ~40% heritable; serotonin, norepinephrine, GABA, HPA axis

cards.prompt: Mild anxiety
cards.answerHtml:
Looks like: perceptual field widens; alert; restless, irritable; names the anxiety easily

Learning: can learn and see relationships

Nursing: use the energy to encourage learning

cards.prompt: Moderate anxiety
cards.answerHtml:
Looks like: field narrows slightly; selective inattention; faster heart and respirations, sweating, muscle tension, faster louder speech; can say "I am anxious"

Nursing: encourage the patient to talk; focus on one experience and describe it

cards.prompt: Severe anxiety
cards.answerHtml:
Looks like: field greatly reduced; fixed on small details; distorted inferences; headache, dizziness, nausea, trembling, palpitations, hyperventilation; may not name the anxiety

Nursing:

  • allow relief behaviors without asking about them
  • encourage talking to bring it down to moderate
  • reduce anxiety first; patient cannot learn

cards.prompt: Panic anxiety
cards.answerHtml:
Looks like: field reduced to a blown-up detail; learning impossible; dissociation, unreality; dilated pupils, labored breathing, trembling, diaphoresis, pallor; may mobilize as rage or pacing

Nursing:

  • safety first; stay with the patient
  • calm, quiet, low stimulation; allow pacing
  • direct short phrases ("Drink this")
  • do not touch
  • anxiolytic when ordered

cards.prompt: Coping: problem-focused vs emotion-focused
cards.answerHtml:
• Problem-focused: changes or removes the stressor (turn off the noisy TV; abused spouse leaves)
  • Emotion-focused: changes the meaning of the situation
  • using emotion-focused when problem-focused is needed is ineffective (abuse victim blames herself)

Positive coping leads to adaptation; negative (alcohol, tobacco, drugs, overeating) leads to maladaptation

Tip: reappraisal occurs after coping

cards.prompt: Defense mechanisms: purpose and nurse's role
cards.answerHtml:
Purpose: reduce anxiety by preventing unwanted thoughts and feelings; mostly unconscious

Healthy or not: can be either; maladaptive when persistent use interferes with function

Nurse: identify the mechanism, judge whether it helps or harms; do not strip a defense from a person in crisis (verify)
cards.label: verify

cards.prompt: Suppression vs repression
cards.answerHtml:
Suppression: conscious decision not to think about it; useful for test taking ("I'll deal with it after my exam")

Repression: unconscious blocking of painful thoughts (cannot recall an assault)

Exam tip: frequent item; conscious vs unconscious

cards.prompt: Displacement vs projection
cards.answerHtml:
Displacement: shifts feeling to a safer target (yelled at by boss, yells at the dog)

Projection: blames others for own unacceptable feelings (wants to cheat, accuses spouse)

Exam tip: displacement changes the target; projection changes who owns the feeling

cards.prompt: Denial, rationalization and reaction formation
cards.answerHtml:
Denial: acts as if the problem is not happening ("I don't have a problem"); common first response to loss, harmful if prolonged

Rationalization: logical excuse for the real reason ("the test was unfair")

Reaction formation: acts opposite to true feeling (overly sweet to a disliked coworker)

cards.prompt: Regression vs intellectualization
cards.answerHtml:
Regression: reverts to earlier, less mature behavior under stress (hospitalized adult throws tantrums)

Intellectualization: detached, analytic; avoids feelings (nurse describes her own cancer only in clinical terms)

Also: fixation = development halted at an immature level, never reached a higher one

cards.prompt: Sublimation, altruism and compensation
cards.answerHtml:
Sublimation: channels an impulse into acceptable behavior (angry teen takes up boxing); generally the most mature

Altruism: helps others to meet own needs (widow volunteers with a grief group)

Compensation: emphasizes a strength to offset a weakness

Tip: sublimation is socially acceptable; substitution is not

cards.prompt: Adjustment disorder
cards.answerHtml:
Looks like: emotional or behavioral symptoms to an identifiable stressor ("situational depression"); onset within 3 months; out of proportion or impairing; common in hospitalized patients

Course: subsides as the situation resolves; no longer than 6 months after the stressor ends

Nursing: assess intensity and coping; problem solving, routines, support; screen for suicide

Tip: persistent or meeting major depression criteria changes the diagnosis

cards.prompt: Psychological factors affecting medical conditions
cards.answerHtml:
Definition: psychological or behavioral factors contribute to development, worsening or delayed recovery of a medical condition; e.g., denial delaying cardiac care (verify)

Evidence:

  • chronic stress suppresses immunity
  • maladaptive anger linked to coronary heart disease; suppressed anger to hypertension and chronic pain
  • Type D personality worsens coronary and diabetes outcomes

Geriatric: chronic stress partly explains poorer health in older adults
cards.label: verify

cards.prompt: Anxiety disorders: risk factors and causes
cards.answerHtml:
Biologic: heritability about 40%; serotonin/norepinephrine and GABA dysregulation; HPA axis

Psychosocial: childhood adversity (ACEs), conditioning to fear, catastrophic misinterpretation of body sensations

Psychodynamic: first attack often follows a loss

At risk: women (2:1), children, chronic illness

Rule out first: thyroid, cardiac, caffeine, stimulants, withdrawal

cards.prompt: Anxiety: primary gain vs secondary gain
cards.answerHtml:
Primary gain: relief of anxiety

Secondary gain: attention and support from being ill

  • can lower motivation to get well

Defense mechanisms: unconscious; healthy (sublimation, altruism, suppression) vs less healthy (denial, projection, displacement, regression, repression)

cards.prompt: Coping strategies for anxiety and stress
cards.answerHtml:
Relaxation: diaphragmatic breathing, progressive muscle relaxation, guided imagery

Cognitive: reframing, positive self-talk, distraction

Acute grounding: 5-4-3-2-1

Lifestyle: exercise, cut caffeine, sleep hygiene

Teach when anxiety is mild. A patient in panic cannot learn new skills.

cards.prompt: Anxiety disorders: how to write an outcome
cards.promptHtml: Anxiety disorders: how to write an outcome
cards.answerHtml:
Good outcome: measurable verb plus a time frame

  • "Names 2 relaxation techniques by day 2"
  • Not measurable: "will not feel anxious"

Long-term examples:

  • panic: fewer attacks, normal activity outside home
  • OCD: less ritual time, Y-BOCS drop 35% or more
  • acute stress disorder: resolves within 1 month

NANDA: anxiety, ineffective coping, fear, powerlessness, post-trauma response

cards.prompt: Panic disorder
cards.answerHtml:
Looks like: sudden attacks peaking in about 10 min; chest pain, dyspnea, fear of dying; then 1 month or more of worry about another

Nursing:

  • stay with patient, short simple phrases, low stimulation, no touch
  • rule out a cardiac cause
  • teach breathing; never say "nothing is wrong"

Treatment: SSRI first-line, CBT, panic control treatment

cards.prompt: Generalized anxiety disorder (GAD)
cards.answerHtml:
Looks like: worry more days than not for 6 months; muscle tension, poor sleep

Tool: GAD-7

Nursing: relaxation, cognitive reframing, sleep teaching; goal is adaptive coping

Treatment: CBT, SSRI/SNRI, buspirone

cards.prompt: Phobias
cards.answerHtml:
Looks like: irrational fear with avoidance

  • types: specific (most common), social anxiety, agoraphobia

Nursing: fear hierarchy, graded exposure

  • blood-injection phobia: watch for vasovagal fainting

Treatment: exposure therapy (first-line); SSRI for social anxiety

cards.prompt: Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD)
cards.answerHtml:
Looks like: obsessions (thoughts) and compulsions (rituals) taking over 1 hour/day; ego-dystonic

Nursing:

  • do not block rituals abruptly at first
  • set a time-limited ritual schedule
  • skin care, consistent staff

Treatment: SSRI plus exposure and response prevention (ERP); TMS

cards.prompt: OCD: how to measure improvement
cards.answerHtml:
Tool: Y-BOCS

Response: drop of 35% or more

Outcomes: reduced ritual time; back to work and normal activities

Timeline: medication effect takes 10-12 weeks; treatment continues 1-2 years

Doses: OCD doses run higher than for depression

Add-on: low-dose antipsychotics only augment refractory OCD

cards.prompt: PTSD
cards.answerHtml:
Looks like (over 1 month):

  • intrusion (flashbacks, nightmares)
  • avoidance
  • negative mood and thoughts
  • hyperarousal

Nursing: safety and suicide screen, trauma-informed care, patient sets the pace, avoid alcohol

Treatment: CBT, EMDR; sertraline or paroxetine; prazosin off-label for nightmares

Not recommended: benzodiazepines

cards.prompt: PTSD: acute vs chronic vs delayed onset
cards.promptHtml: PTSD: acute vs chronic vs delayed onset
cards.answerHtml:
Acute: symptoms about 1 month after trauma

Chronic: 3 months or more

Delayed onset: more than 6 months after the trauma (lecture value; Boyd says "up to 6 months later")

Risk factors: prior acute stress disorder, severity and duration of trauma, low self-esteem, poor resilience

In children: reactive attachment disorder, disinhibited social engagement disorder

cards.prompt: Acute stress disorder vs PTSD
cards.answerHtml:
ASD: PTSD-like symptoms that resolve within 1 month of the trauma

PTSD: symptoms last over 1 month

Nursing for ASD: safety, sleep, support, short-term coping help

Note: ASD may progress to PTSD

cards.prompt: Panic attack vs anxiety attack
cards.answerHtml:
Panic attack: sudden, peaks in about 10 min; onset of panic disorder typically age 20-24

"Anxiety attack": builds over hours to months (not a DSM term)

Acute-phase care:

  • stay, reassure of safety
  • breathing and 5-4-3-2-1 grounding
  • reduce stimulation, no touch
  • screen for suicidal ideation (about 1 in 5)
  • PRN medication

cards.prompt: Anxiety disorders: treatment overview (not drug profiles)
cards.answerHtml:
First-line long term: SSRI or SNRI (4-6 weeks to full effect, early jitteriness, suicidality warning in the young, never stop abruptly)

Short term only: benzodiazepines for severe anxiety, taper, never combine with alcohol

Therapy: CBT, exposure/ERP, relaxation

Setting: outpatient, least restrictive; admit for suicide risk or medication change

cards.prompt: Older adults with anxiety
cards.answerHtml:
Looks like: as common as depression; hides behind pain and somatic complaints

Nursing:

  • screen for suicide risk
  • avoid benzodiazepines (falls, confusion, respiratory depression)
  • build the plan on strengths, family support, wellness

cards.prompt: Anxiety care: community, case management, trends
cards.answerHtml:
Setting: mostly outpatient; nurses run relaxation and medication-monitoring groups, home visits

Case management: integrated primary-care follow-up limits polypharmacy

EBP: CBT, exposure/ERP, panic control treatment, relaxation, yoga, mindfulness

Trends: TMS for OCD, telehealth and apps, virtual-reality exposure, ACT, service dogs

cards.prompt: Anxiety disorders: which disorder, which first-line care?
cards.promptHtml: Anxiety disorders: which disorder, which first-line care?
cards.answerHtml:
Panic: SSRI, breathing, no touch

GAD: CBT, relaxation, reframing

Phobia: exposure hierarchy

OCD: SSRI plus ERP, do not block rituals abruptly

PTSD: safety and trust first; avoid benzodiazepines

ASD: safety, sleep, support

cards.prompt: Crisis: definition and phases
cards.answerHtml:
Definition: time-limited event where usual coping fails; resolves in about 6 weeks (ATI: 4-6); there is no chronic crisis

Phases:

  • 1: anxiety rises, defenses used
  • 2: defenses fail, disorganization
  • 3: severe anxiety or panic, flight
  • 4: overwhelmed, powerless; risk of violence to self or others

Turning point: growth or deterioration

cards.prompt: Types of crisis
cards.answerHtml:
Maturational (developmental): leaving home, marriage, retirement

Situational: specific event (illness, job loss, divorce, even positive change)

Adventitious (traumatic/social): disaster, violent crime, mass trauma

Note: lecture says developmental/situational/traumatic; same categories

cards.prompt: Crisis theory and principles
cards.answerHtml:
Caplan: disequilibrium when problem solving fails

Erikson: developmental crisis

Principles:

  • goal is pre-crisis functioning
  • here-and-now, solution-focused
  • nurse is active and directive
  • use strengths and supports
  • refer when coping or support is inadequate

cards.prompt: Suicide and homicide: bio-psychosocial causes
cards.answerHtml:
Biologic: low serotonin, HPA dysfunction, depression

Psychologic: hopelessness, thwarted belonging, perceived burden

Social: isolation, contagion, economic stress

Predictors: prior attempt (strongest), substance use, agitation, firearm access, giving away possessions

cards.prompt: Crisis: nursing priorities in order
cards.answerHtml:
1. Physical: injury, ABCs, basic needs

2. Safety: assess suicidal and homicidal risk immediately

3. Assess: emotions, coping, social support, spiritual needs

4. Communicate: empathy, silence, reflecting; no false reassurance, one problem at a time

5. Intervene and refer: sleep, food, hotlines, short-term medication

cards.prompt: Nurse self-awareness and vicarious traumatization
cards.answerHtml:
Self-awareness: examine your own feelings about suicide, anger and loss

Vicarious (secondary) traumatization: caring for suicidal or assaulted patients can traumatize the nurse

Do: debrief, talk with peers, use counseling

After assaults: document every incident

cards.prompt: Grief as a crisis
cards.answerHtml:
Bereavement can itself be a crisis

Nursing: normalize sadness and yearning; do not just reassure

  • refer to counseling or support groups

No fixed stages: dual process model is nonlinear

Prolonged grief disorder: longing lasting over 6 months

cards.prompt: Crisis care: community, case management, tangible support
cards.promptHtml: Crisis care: community, case management, tangible support
cards.answerHtml:
Tangible support: food, shelter, transport, hotline numbers

Case management: no discharge until follow-up is arranged and means are secured

Services: telephone hotlines, residential crisis units

After disaster: psychological first aid (ABCs: arousal, behavior, cognition); compulsory debriefing not recommended

cards.prompt: Suicide in crisis: secrecy, tool, documentation
cards.answerHtml:
Never promise secrecy; you are a mandated reporter

Ask about: ideation, plan, intent, availability and lethality of means

Tool: C-SSRS

Document: history, intent, plan, means, substance use

Risk factors and IS PATH WARM: Unit 7 cards

cards.prompt: Imminent suicide risk: safety plan and long-term care
cards.promptHtml: Imminent suicide risk: safety plan and long-term care
cards.answerHtml:
Setting: safety in the least restrictive setting

Use: a safety plan and a commitment to treatment statement (not a no-suicide contract)

Long term:

  • treat the underlying disorder (SSRI; clozapine is approved for suicide risk in schizophrenia)
  • ECT, support groups

Discharge: follow-up arranged, means secured

Unit precautions (hazards, observation): Unit 7 cards

cards.prompt: Anger and aggression: de-escalation
cards.answerHtml:
Do:

  • calm, nonthreatening body language, personal space, exit access
  • listen and validate
  • give concrete choices
  • reduce stimulation
  • offer PRN medication

Last resort: seclusion or restraint

Restraint rules: RN verifies need; provider examines within 1 hour

cards.prompt: Anger management vs CBT for anger
cards.answerHtml:
Anger management: psychoeducation, 4-10 weekly sessions, leader acts as teacher and coach; for non-violent anger

CBT: for chronic anger

Meds for acute agitation: PRN antipsychotic (olanzapine, ziprasidone preferred over haloperidol) or benzodiazepine

cards.prompt: Violence and abuse: reporting duties
cards.answerHtml:
Mandated reporting: suspected child, older-adult or vulnerable-adult abuse

Duty to warn (Tarasoff): foreseeable victim of a patient's violence

Homicide risk: observation, documentation, Danger Assessment tool

Cycle of violence: tension building, acute battering, honeymoon

cards.prompt: Delirium vs dementia
cards.answerHtml:
Delirium: sudden onset (hours to days); fluctuating, worse at night; consciousness reduced; attention impaired; usually reversible

Dementia: insidious; stable (sundowning possible); consciousness clear; progressive, not reversible

Key: differ by cause and course, not symptoms

They coexist: a sudden worsening in dementia means a delirium workup

cards.prompt: Depression vs dementia (pseudodementia)
cards.answerHtml:
Depression: onset weeks to months, often after loss; worse in the morning (verify); complains of memory loss ("I don't know"); reversible with treatment

Dementia: insidious; patient unaware of deficits, may confabulate; progressive

Pseudodementia: depression that looks like dementia; reverses with treatment

Risk: depression is the greatest suicide risk factor in older adults
cards.label: verify

cards.prompt: Sudden confusion in an older adult: what first?
cards.promptHtml: Sudden confusion in an older adult: what first?
cards.answerHtml:
Think delirium (medical emergency) until proven otherwise

Check: vital signs, glucose, oxygen, medications (anticholinergics), infection (UTI, pneumonia), pain, electrolytes

Do not label it dementia or "disease progression"

Get family's account of baseline vs now

cards.prompt: Delirium: findings and risk factors
cards.answerHtml:
Looks like: fluctuating consciousness; cannot focus or shift attention; impaired recent memory; disoriented to time and place, rarely to person; incoherent speech; restless then lethargic; visual hallucinations

Risk factors: older age, dementia, infection, electrolyte imbalance, anticholinergic drugs, pain, alcohol withdrawal, new long-term care admission

Subtypes: hyperactive, hypoactive (most common), mixed

cards.prompt: Delirium: nursing care
cards.answerHtml:
First: find and treat the cause; stop suspect drugs

Nursing:

  • vitals at least every 2 hours
  • balance fluids and electrolytes, offer oral fluids
  • orientation cues, glasses, hearing aids, sleep, early mobilization
  • low bed, supervision; avoid restraints

Meds: none treats delirium; low-dose antipsychotic only for hallucinations/delusions; benzodiazepines for alcohol withdrawal

cards.prompt: Neurocognitive disorders: DSM-5-TR categories
cards.answerHtml:
Three diagnoses: delirium, mild NCD (MCI), major NCD (dementia)

MCI: modest decline, ADLs kept; amnestic (forgets events) vs nonamnestic (judgment, sequencing)

Domains: attention, executive function, memory, language, perceptual-motor, social cognition

Terms: aphasia, anomia, agraphia, alexia, apraxia, agnosia

cards.prompt: Alzheimer disease
cards.answerHtml:
Looks like: insidious, progressive; first loses new learning, then word-finding, then aphasia; poor judgment, personality change, delusions (theft, impostors)

Cause: amyloid plaques, tau tangles

Dx: clinical; confirmed only at autopsy

Types: early-onset (65 or younger, faster), late-onset (over 65)

cards.prompt: Other dementias: how to tell them apart
cards.promptHtml: Other dementias: how to tell them apart
cards.answerHtml:
Vascular: step-wise decline after small strokes/TIAs; control HTN, diabetes

Lewy body: visual hallucinations, REM sleep disorder, parkinsonism, fluctuating; very sensitive to antipsychotics

Frontotemporal: apathy or disinhibition, little insight

CJD (prion): rapidly fatal; tremor, seizures; no treatment

Also: Parkinson, Huntington (chorea), HIV, TBI

cards.prompt: Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome
cards.answerHtml:
Cause: thiamine (B1) deficiency, usually chronic alcohol use

Wernicke (acute): confusion, ataxia, eye changes

Korsakoff (chronic amnestic): amnesia, cannot learn new information, confabulation

Treat: thiamine now; give it before or with any glucose, never after (verify)
cards.label: verify

cards.prompt: Dementia: stage-based nursing priorities
cards.answerHtml:
Early: support and cognition

Middle: safety

Late: physical needs

Staging tools: FAST, Global Deterioration Scale

Family: 60-70% with AD live at home; most care is by family

cards.prompt: Cognitive assessment tools
cards.answerHtml:
Delirium: CAM, NEECHAM

Cognitive screens: MoCA, MMSE, Mini-Cog, SLUMS

Family interview: AD8

Staging: FAST, Global Deterioration Scale

Long-term care: BIMS

Workup: labs, imaging rule out other causes (electrolytes, folate, B12, thyroid, UA)

cards.prompt: MMSE and SPMSQ scoring
cards.answerHtml:
MMSE: 24-30 no impairment; 18-23 mild; 0-17 severe; below 24 abnormal

SPMSQ (10 questions):

  • 0-2 errors normal
  • 3-4 mild
  • 5-7 moderate
  • 8+ severe
  • allow 1 more error with grade-school education or less, 1 fewer beyond high school

cards.prompt: Dementia: communication and behavior
cards.answerHtml:
Memory/orientation: clocks, calendars, reminiscence; do not argue about the date, redirect

Delusions: nonconfrontation; "Do you want to see if anything is missing?"

Agitation: calm approach, do not reason; check pain, toileting, hunger, overstimulation

Language: supply the word at once

cards.prompt: Dementia: which drugs to limit or avoid?
cards.promptHtml: Dementia: which drugs to limit or avoid?
cards.answerHtml:
Anticholinergics: avoid all

Antipsychotics: off-label for dementia-related psychosis; boxed warning: higher death risk in older adults

Benzodiazepines: short-term only

NSAIDs: GI bleeding

Rule: start low, go slow

Donepezil, memantine and other dementia drugs: Medications cards

cards.prompt: Dementia: home safety and community care
cards.answerHtml:
Home safety: remove scatter rugs, lock cleaning supplies, lower water heater, mark stair edges, ID bracelet, locks that are hard to open

Resources: adult day care, respite, home health aides, meal delivery, support groups

Case management: continuity across settings

cards.prompt: Family caregivers and staff attitudes
cards.answerHtml:
Behavior is communication of an unmet need

Avoid: childlike language (ageist), calling the patient "difficult"

Caregivers: exhausted, isolated, trapped; abuse risk if patient agitated

Nurse: assess caregiver, refer to support group, respite, adult day care; self-assess your own frustration first

Autonomy: include the patient in decisions

cards.prompt: Somatic symptom disorder (SSD)
cards.answerHtml:
Looks like: real symptoms (often pain) 6 months or more, with excessive thoughts, anxiety or time spent on them; may or may not be medically explained

Features: chronic, onset before 30, provider shopping, secondary gain, not under conscious control

Note: "somatoform" is the old term

cards.prompt: Illness anxiety disorder
cards.answerHtml:
Looks like: fear of having a serious illness from misread body sensations; few or no symptoms; reassurance fails; 6 months or more

Old name: hypochondriasis

Nursing: one provider, scheduled visits, acknowledge fear, link stress to symptoms

cards.prompt: Conversion disorder (functional neurologic symptom disorder)
cards.answerHtml:
Looks like: loss of voluntary motor or sensory function (paralysis, blindness, aphonia, nonepileptic seizures) with negative tests; follows the patient's idea of the problem, not anatomy

May show: la belle indifference; most remit without treatment

Nursing: accept symptoms as real, do not confront

cards.prompt: Pain disorder and body dysmorphic disorder
cards.answerHtml:
Pain disorder: pain is the central focus of life, causing distress and impaired function; now classified as SSD with predominant pain (verify)

Body dysmorphic disorder: preoccupation with a perceived flaw in appearance (verify); taught in the lecture's somatic group

Nursing: believe the pain is real; nonpharmacologic pain relief
cards.label: verify

cards.prompt: Somatic symptom disorders: nursing care
cards.answerHtml:
Assess: let patient describe every physical problem first; OTC meds, trauma, suicide risk

Relationship: trust and believing; one provider, scheduled visits, symptom journal

Redirect, don't dismiss: acknowledge symptom, link stress, shift to coping

Teach: relaxation, exercise, problem-solving

Meds: treat comorbid depression/anxiety (SSRI/SNRI); avoid benzodiazepines

Therapy: CBT

cards.prompt: Somatic symptom disorders: what NOT to do
cards.promptHtml: Somatic symptom disorders: what NOT to do
cards.answerHtml:
Do not say "it's all in your head"

Do not stop the physical workup because of an SSD label

Do not confront an SSD or conversion patient about faking

Do not give unsupervised polypharmacy; track all medication use

Case management: follow-up visits every 4-6 weeks reduce unscheduled care

cards.prompt: Factitious disorder vs malingering
cards.answerHtml:
Factitious: symptoms intentionally produced to be a patient (sick role); no outside reward; psychiatric disorder
