Ignore the behavior and continue care D. State calmly that the behavior is uncomfortable and does not fit a professional relationship
cards.promptHtml:
A hospitalized patient with histrionic personality disorder compliments the nurse's appearance, touches the nurse's arm and says, "I feel we have a special bond." Which response best maintains the therapeutic relationship?

  • A. Laugh it off and change the subject
  • B. Ask the unit manager to reassign the patient permanently
  • C. Ignore the behavior and continue care
  • D. State calmly that the behavior is uncomfortable and does not fit a professional relationship
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: D

Boundary violations should be addressed promptly, calmly and without taking them personally, by naming the behavior and describing the professional nature of the relationship. Laughing it off (A) or ignoring it (C) sends mixed messages. Permanent reassignment (B) is an overreaction and does not teach appropriate limits. The goal is to promote autonomy and avoid meeting social needs through care.

cards.prompt: A nurse teaches nursing students about impulse-control disorders. Which statements are accurate? Select all that apply. A. Tension builds before the behavior and is released with a pleasurable effect. B. Regret or remorse often follows the behavior. C. People with kleptomania steal items they need and cannot afford. D. Treatment is usually long-term outpatient therapy, often with group sessions. E. In intermittent explosive disorder, the aggression is proportionate to the provocation.
cards.promptHtml:
A nurse teaches nursing students about impulse-control disorders. Which statements are accurate? Select all that apply.

  • A. Tension builds before the behavior and is released with a pleasurable effect.
  • B. Regret or remorse often follows the behavior.
  • C. People with kleptomania steal items they need and cannot afford.
  • D. Treatment is usually long-term outpatient therapy, often with group sessions.
  • E. In intermittent explosive disorder, the aggression is proportionate to the provocation.
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: A, B, D

Impulse-control disorders follow a cycle of rising tension, release or gratification, then remorse, and are usually treated with long-term outpatient and group therapy. In kleptomania the person steals items that are not needed and could usually be afforded; the act itself is the point. In IED, aggression is out of proportion to the provocation, which is why it is diagnosed only after other causes are excluded.

cards.prompt: A nurse reviews the history of four patients who have set fires. Which patient's history best fits a diagnosis of pyromania? A. A man who feels rising tension, is fascinated by fire, feels gratification when fires burn and has no other motive B. A woman who set fire to her ex-partner's car out of anger C. A teenager who set a fire as part of a group protest D. A man with psychosis who set a fire because voices commanded it
cards.promptHtml:
A nurse reviews the history of four patients who have set fires. Which patient's history best fits a diagnosis of pyromania?

  • A. A man who feels rising tension, is fascinated by fire, feels gratification when fires burn and has no other motive
  • B. A woman who set fire to her ex-partner's car out of anger
  • C. A teenager who set a fire as part of a group protest
  • D. A man with psychosis who set a fire because voices commanded it
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: A

Pyromania involves repeated fire setting with tension or arousal beforehand, fascination with fire and gratification during or after. It is not motivated by anger, revenge, political ideology or suicide, and it is not diagnosed when psychosis explains the act (general knowledge). The other patients had a clear motive (B, C) or a psychotic cause (D). CBT targeting self-esteem, interpersonal skills and coping is the lecture's treatment.

cards.prompt: A 22-year-old man with borderline personality disorder, being discharged after a suicide attempt, asks his primary nurse to meet with him "for just a few sessions" because his therapist is on vacation. Which response is best? A. Agree to meet for two sessions to keep him safe B. Say that the relationship ends today and wish him well C. Acknowledge his worry about being alone, explain the nurse's role limits and help arrange coverage by another clinician D. Tell him he should not need extra support
cards.promptHtml:
A 22-year-old man with borderline personality disorder, being discharged after a suicide attempt, asks his primary nurse to meet with him "for just a few sessions" because his therapist is on vacation. Which response is best?

  • A. Agree to meet for two sessions to keep him safe
  • B. Say that the relationship ends today and wish him well
  • C. Acknowledge his worry about being alone, explain the nurse's role limits and help arrange coverage by another clinician
  • D. Tell him he should not need extra support
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: C

The request reflects fear of abandonment at termination. The nurse validates the feeling, keeps the professional role and boundary, and helps the patient identify other supports and covering clinicians before discharge. Extending the relationship (A) breaks the boundary and may reinforce dependence. An abrupt, casual ending (B) or dismissing the need (D) triggers abandonment fears and raises suicide risk.

cards.prompt: After the wound care is complete, a patient with borderline personality disorder who cut herself after a phone argument is calm. Which nursing statement is most therapeutic? A. "You must not do this again, or the team will limit your privileges." B. "Tell me what was happening just before you felt the urge to cut." C. "I'm sure you know cutting only makes things worse." D. "Let's not discuss it so you can rest."
cards.promptHtml:
After the wound care is complete, a patient with borderline personality disorder who cut herself after a phone argument is calm. Which nursing statement is most therapeutic?

  • A. "You must not do this again, or the team will limit your privileges."
  • B. "Tell me what was happening just before you felt the urge to cut."
  • C. "I'm sure you know cutting only makes things worse."
  • D. "Let's not discuss it so you can rest."
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: B

Once the patient is safe, the nurse explores antecedents and feelings nonjudgmentally and plans alternatives such as self-soothing skills, since self-harm often relieves emotional pain. Threatening privileges (A) and lecturing (C) are punitive and shame the patient. Avoiding the topic (D) misses the chance to prevent the next episode.

cards.prompt: Which features are required for a pattern of behavior to be considered a personality disorder? Select all that apply. A. It is enduring and stable over time. B. It begins in adolescence or early adulthood. C. It occurs only during episodes of substance intoxication. D. It is pervasive and inflexible across situations. E. It causes distress or impairment.
cards.promptHtml:
Which features are required for a pattern of behavior to be considered a personality disorder? Select all that apply.

  • A. It is enduring and stable over time.
  • B. It begins in adolescence or early adulthood.
  • C. It occurs only during episodes of substance intoxication.
  • D. It is pervasive and inflexible across situations.
  • E. It causes distress or impairment.
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: A, B, D, E

A personality disorder is an enduring, stable pattern that deviates from cultural expectations, is pervasive and inflexible, starts in adolescence or early adulthood and causes distress or impairment. A pattern limited to substance intoxication (C) would be explained by the substance and does not meet the definition of a personality disorder.

cards.prompt: A nurse is caring for a patient with schizoid personality disorder who spends most of the day alone. Which care plan priority is most appropriate? A. Offer social skills training with a gradual, tolerable level of social activity B. Require attendance at all group activities C. Leave the patient alone since the isolation is preferred D. Confront the patient about lacking empathy
cards.promptHtml:
A nurse is caring for a patient with schizoid personality disorder who spends most of the day alone. Which care plan priority is most appropriate?

  • A. Offer social skills training with a gradual, tolerable level of social activity
  • B. Require attendance at all group activities
  • C. Leave the patient alone since the isolation is preferred
  • D. Confront the patient about lacking empathy
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: A

Care for schizoid personality disorder targets poor social relations and low self-esteem. Social skills training builds the ability to relate, and the nurse aims for a middle ground: enough contact to keep the patient from withdrawing completely, but not so much that it overwhelms. Mandatory groups (B) overshoot that balance. Leaving the patient alone (C) lets isolation deepen. Confronting the patient (D) damages an already fragile relationship.

cards.prompt: A nurse reviews admission data for a 17-year-old with anorexia nervosa. Which finding should the nurse report to the provider first? A. Fine, downy hair over the back and arms B. Absence of menstrual periods for 6 months C. Heart rate of 38 beats/min with a potassium of 2.8 mEq/L and a prolonged QT interval D. A BMI of 15.5 kg/m2 and a perfectionistic personality
cards.promptHtml:
A nurse reviews admission data for a 17-year-old with anorexia nervosa. Which finding should the nurse report to the provider first?

  • A. Fine, downy hair over the back and arms
  • B. Absence of menstrual periods for 6 months
  • C. Heart rate of 38 beats/min with a potassium of 2.8 mEq/L and a prolonged QT interval
  • D. A BMI of 15.5 kg/m2 and a perfectionistic personality
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: C

Medical instability and cardiac risk come first. Severe bradycardia, hypokalemia and QT prolongation can cause fatal ventricular arrhythmias, and Boyd states cardiac issues are treated before the psychological issues. Lanugo and amenorrhea are expected starvation findings that need follow-up but are not immediately life-threatening. A BMI of 15.5 is severe but chronic, and perfectionism is a personality trait, not an emergency.

cards.prompt: On day 3 of refeeding, a patient with anorexia nervosa has a serum phosphorus of 1.2 mg/dL, new ankle edema, a heart rate of 118 beats/min and mild shortness of breath. Which action should the nurse take first? A. Encourage the patient to drink more fluids to flush the electrolytes B. Notify the provider immediately, apply cardiac monitoring and hold further calorie increases until directed C. Offer a high-carbohydrate snack to raise energy D. Reassure the patient that these changes are a normal part of weight gain
cards.promptHtml:
On day 3 of refeeding, a patient with anorexia nervosa has a serum phosphorus of 1.2 mg/dL, new ankle edema, a heart rate of 118 beats/min and mild shortness of breath. Which action should the nurse take first?

  • A. Encourage the patient to drink more fluids to flush the electrolytes
  • B. Notify the provider immediately, apply cardiac monitoring and hold further calorie increases until directed
  • C. Offer a high-carbohydrate snack to raise energy
  • D. Reassure the patient that these changes are a normal part of weight gain
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: B

These findings suggest refeeding syndrome: low phosphate, fluid overload, tachycardia and early respiratory compromise. It can progress to cardiac and respiratory failure and sudden death, so the nurse reports at once, monitors and awaits orders on feeding rate and electrolyte replacement. Extra fluids or carbohydrate worsen the shift and overload. Calling these findings normal delays treatment.

cards.prompt: A patient with anorexia nervosa begins an inpatient refeeding protocol. Which findings would the nurse recognize as features of refeeding syndrome? Select all that apply. A. Hypophosphatemia B. Hypokalemia C. Hypermagnesemia D. Circulatory fluid overload with peripheral edema E. Hypernatremia with dry mucous membranes
cards.promptHtml:
A patient with anorexia nervosa begins an inpatient refeeding protocol. Which findings would the nurse recognize as features of refeeding syndrome? Select all that apply.

  • A. Hypophosphatemia
  • B. Hypokalemia
  • C. Hypermagnesemia
  • D. Circulatory fluid overload with peripheral edema
  • E. Hypernatremia with dry mucous membranes
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: A, B, D

Refeeding syndrome occurs when the body shifts back to carbohydrate metabolism and phosphorus, potassium and magnesium are driven into cells, so levels fall. Hypophosphatemia comes first. Fluid overload, respiratory failure and cardiac failure follow. Magnesium falls rather than rises (option C is wrong). Hypernatremia with dehydration is not the typical pattern; sodium and water retention cause edema instead.

cards.prompt: A patient with bulimia nervosa who has been using laxatives daily asks why the laxatives have not helped lasting weight loss. Which nurse teaching statement, if repeated by the patient, shows the teaching was effective? A. "Laxatives remove calories from my stomach before they can be absorbed." B. "Laxatives work well if I take them only after a very large binge." C. "Laxatives are safe as long as I drink extra coffee to stay hydrated." D. "Laxatives only cause water loss from the colon and can drop my potassium to a dangerous level."
cards.promptHtml:
A patient with bulimia nervosa who has been using laxatives daily asks why the laxatives have not helped lasting weight loss. Which nurse teaching statement, if repeated by the patient, shows the teaching was effective?

  • A. "Laxatives remove calories from my stomach before they can be absorbed."
  • B. "Laxatives work well if I take them only after a very large binge."
  • C. "Laxatives are safe as long as I drink extra coffee to stay hydrated."
  • D. "Laxatives only cause water loss from the colon and can drop my potassium to a dangerous level."
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: D

Laxatives act on the colon, but food is absorbed higher in the gastrointestinal tract in the stomach and small intestine, so they cause only temporary water-weight loss. They also cause dehydration and potassium depletion, which can trigger arrhythmias. Options A and B repeat the myth the nurse is correcting. Caffeine can worsen fluid loss and is discouraged.

cards.prompt: A hospitalized patient with anorexia nervosa looks at the nurse and says, "Can't you see I'm fat? Everyone is lying to me." Which response by the nurse is best? A. "I know it feels that way to you, and it sounds frightening. I see your body differently, and I am worried about your health." B. "Look at your arms and ribs. You are far too thin." C. "Why do you believe nobody is telling you the truth?" D. "You are not fat. Let's not talk about it."
cards.promptHtml:
A hospitalized patient with anorexia nervosa looks at the nurse and says, "Can't you see I'm fat? Everyone is lying to me." Which response by the nurse is best?

  • A. "I know it feels that way to you, and it sounds frightening. I see your body differently, and I am worried about your health."
  • B. "Look at your arms and ribs. You are far too thin."
  • C. "Why do you believe nobody is telling you the truth?"
  • D. "You are not fat. Let's not talk about it."
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: A

Body image distortion is often the last symptom to resolve, so arguing or pointing out thinness does not change it. The nurse acknowledges the feeling, states a differing view calmly and keeps the focus on health. Option B is confrontational. "Why" questions (C) can sound accusing and are less therapeutic. Option D shuts down the patient's feelings.

cards.prompt: An inpatient with bulimia nervosa hands back an empty dinner tray and tells the nurse, "My stomach looks huge now. I hate the way I look after every meal." Which nurse action is best? A. Praise her for finishing the meal and leave so she can have some privacy B. Tell her the bathroom will stay locked because staff cannot trust her alone C. Validate how uncomfortable she feels and offer to spend the next hour with her in a planned activity D. Explain that vomiting will lower her potassium and harm her heart
cards.promptHtml:
An inpatient with bulimia nervosa hands back an empty dinner tray and tells the nurse, "My stomach looks huge now. I hate the way I look after every meal." Which nurse action is best?

  • A. Praise her for finishing the meal and leave so she can have some privacy
  • B. Tell her the bathroom will stay locked because staff cannot trust her alone
  • C. Validate how uncomfortable she feels and offer to spend the next hour with her in a planned activity
  • D. Explain that vomiting will lower her potassium and harm her heart
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: C

The urge to purge peaks in the period right after a meal. Accepting the feeling without judgment and offering supervised company through that window supports her and blocks purging, which is part of the care plan. Leaving her alone (A) removes support when risk is highest. An accusing, unexplained restriction (B) damages trust and invites a power struggle. Lecturing about complications at a moment of distress (D) does not help her resist the urge.

cards.prompt: A nurse is reviewing the status of several outpatients with eating disorders. Which findings meet criteria for hospital admission? Select all that apply. A. Heart rate of 40 beats/min B. Blood pressure of 76/48 mm Hg C. Suicidal ideation with a plan D. BMI of 18.5 with stable vital signs and normal labs E. Serum phosphorus below the normal range
cards.promptHtml:
A nurse is reviewing the status of several outpatients with eating disorders. Which findings meet criteria for hospital admission? Select all that apply.

  • A. Heart rate of 40 beats/min
  • B. Blood pressure of 76/48 mm Hg
  • C. Suicidal ideation with a plan
  • D. BMI of 18.5 with stable vital signs and normal labs
  • E. Serum phosphorus below the normal range
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: A, B, C, E

Boyd's hospitalization criteria include a heart rate near 40, blood pressure below 80/50, temperature below 36.1 C, weight below 85% of ideal, hypokalemia, hypophosphatemia, hypomagnesemia, and psychiatric risks such as suicide and severe depression. A BMI of 18.5 with stable vital signs and normal labs fits outpatient management.

cards.prompt: A provider orders fluoxetine for a patient with bulimia nervosa. Which information should the nurse include when teaching the patient? A. "This drug works immediately to stop binge eating." B. "It is often given at a higher dose for eating disorders, and it may take several weeks to reach full effect." C. "Take it at bedtime to prevent insomnia." D. "You can stop it as soon as the binges stop."
cards.promptHtml:
A provider orders fluoxetine for a patient with bulimia nervosa. Which information should the nurse include when teaching the patient?

  • A. "This drug works immediately to stop binge eating."
  • B. "It is often given at a higher dose for eating disorders, and it may take several weeks to reach full effect."
  • C. "Take it at bedtime to prevent insomnia."
  • D. "You can stop it as soon as the binges stop."
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: B

Fluoxetine is FDA-approved for bulimia nervosa and reduces binge and vomiting episodes. The usual eating-disorder dose is higher (about 60 mg/day), and the full effect can take up to 4 weeks. It is given in the morning because it can cause insomnia, and it should not be stopped without the provider.

cards.prompt: A patient with anorexia nervosa has severe meal-time anxiety, and the provider prescribes olanzapine. The patient asks, "Is this approved for anorexia?" Which response by the nurse is most accurate? A. "Yes, olanzapine is the FDA-approved first-line drug for anorexia." B. "Yes, fluoxetine and olanzapine are both approved, and you will take them together." C. "No, because it is a sedative that treats only anxiety." D. "No drug is FDA-approved for anorexia. Olanzapine is used to help with weight gain, anxiety and intense eating-disorder thoughts."
cards.promptHtml:
A patient with anorexia nervosa has severe meal-time anxiety, and the provider prescribes olanzapine. The patient asks, "Is this approved for anorexia?" Which response by the nurse is most accurate?

  • A. "Yes, olanzapine is the FDA-approved first-line drug for anorexia."
  • B. "Yes, fluoxetine and olanzapine are both approved, and you will take them together."
  • C. "No, because it is a sedative that treats only anxiety."
  • D. "No drug is FDA-approved for anorexia. Olanzapine is used to help with weight gain, anxiety and intense eating-disorder thoughts."
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: D

The lecture states that no medication is FDA-approved for anorexia nervosa. Olanzapine, an atypical antipsychotic, is used off-label to promote weight gain and reduce anxiety and obsessive eating-disorder thoughts, often with an SSRI for comorbid illness. Options A and B are incorrect. It is not a sedative (C). Boyd's statement that fluoxetine is approved for AN conflicts with the lecture and is not accepted here.

cards.prompt: A patient with binge-eating disorder is prescribed lisdexamfetamine. Which history should the nurse report to the provider before the first dose? A. Cocaine use disorder B. Childhood obesity C. Distress after binge episodes D. Perfectionism
cards.promptHtml:
A patient with binge-eating disorder is prescribed lisdexamfetamine. Which history should the nurse report to the provider before the first dose?

  • A. Cocaine use disorder
  • B. Childhood obesity
  • C. Distress after binge episodes
  • D. Perfectionism
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: A

Lisdexamfetamine is a CNS stimulant used in BED that is habit-forming and may not be recommended for patients with a substance use disorder. Childhood obesity, distress after binges and perfectionism are risk factors or features of BED, not contraindications. The nurse reports the history because misuse risk changes the prescriber's choice, and teaches that the drug is not a weight-loss product.

cards.prompt: A nurse assesses a normal-weight patient who admits to self-induced vomiting after binge eating. Which findings would the nurse expect? Select all that apply. A. Parotid gland enlargement B. Erosion of dental enamel C. Hypokalemia D. Calluses on the knuckles E. Lanugo covering the back
cards.promptHtml:
A nurse assesses a normal-weight patient who admits to self-induced vomiting after binge eating. Which findings would the nurse expect? Select all that apply.

  • A. Parotid gland enlargement
  • B. Erosion of dental enamel
  • C. Hypokalemia
  • D. Calluses on the knuckles
  • E. Lanugo covering the back
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: A, B, C, D

Self-induced vomiting causes parotid enlargement, enamel erosion, loss of stomach acid (hypochloremic alkalosis and hypokalemia; the lecture slide and Boyd p.1530 print "hyperchloremic," but acid loss lowers chloride), and knuckle calluses from the teeth (Russell sign). Lanugo is a sign of starvation and is not expected in a normal-weight patient who maintains weight by purging.

cards.prompt: A nurse teaches the parents of a daughter newly diagnosed with anorexia nervosa. Which statement by a parent shows understanding? A. "I will watch every bite she takes and tell her when she looks too thin." B. "I will tell her she looks healthier so she feels encouraged." C. "I will avoid comments about her weight and appearance and talk about other things." D. "I will insist that she eat so we can win the power struggle."
cards.promptHtml:
A nurse teaches the parents of a daughter newly diagnosed with anorexia nervosa. Which statement by a parent shows understanding?

  • A. "I will watch every bite she takes and tell her when she looks too thin."
  • B. "I will tell her she looks healthier so she feels encouraged."
  • C. "I will avoid comments about her weight and appearance and talk about other things."
  • D. "I will insist that she eat so we can win the power struggle."
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: C

Boyd advises family and friends to express concern and care, avoid discussing weight, calories or appearance (praise about weight can feel like criticism), talk about other topics, and avoid power struggles because they cannot force eating. Close monitoring with comments, reassurance that she looks healthier, and forcing eating can all increase conflict and reinforce the disorder.

cards.prompt: A patient with anorexia nervosa who is on bed rest during refeeding says, "You are punishing me by keeping me in bed." Which response is most therapeutic? A. "Rules are rules, and everyone on this unit must follow them." B. "Resting saves energy your body needs to regain weight. The plan is the same for every patient and is meant to help you, not punish you." C. "If you cooperate, I can talk to the doctor about letting you up sooner." D. "It is the doctor's order, and I cannot discuss it."
cards.promptHtml:
A patient with anorexia nervosa who is on bed rest during refeeding says, "You are punishing me by keeping me in bed." Which response is most therapeutic?

  • A. "Rules are rules, and everyone on this unit must follow them."
  • B. "Resting saves energy your body needs to regain weight. The plan is the same for every patient and is meant to help you, not punish you."
  • C. "If you cooperate, I can talk to the doctor about letting you up sooner."
  • D. "It is the doctor's order, and I cannot discuss it."
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: B

The nurse gives the rationale, stresses that the protocol is consistent and nonpunitive, and stays nonreactive. This builds trust and reduces power struggles. Option A is rigid and gives no reason. Option C turns the plan into a bargain that the nurse cannot guarantee. Option D ends communication.

cards.prompt: A 19-year-old patient who is 5 ft 6 in and 150 lb lost 40 lb in 4 months by severely restricting food. She has an intense fear of gaining weight, amenorrhea and a heart rate of 48 beats/min. Which diagnosis best fits? A. Binge-eating disorder B. Avoidant restrictive food intake disorder C. Bulimia nervosa D. Atypical anorexia nervosa
cards.promptHtml:
A 19-year-old patient who is 5 ft 6 in and 150 lb lost 40 lb in 4 months by severely restricting food. She has an intense fear of gaining weight, amenorrhea and a heart rate of 48 beats/min. Which diagnosis best fits?

  • A. Binge-eating disorder
  • B. Avoidant restrictive food intake disorder
  • C. Bulimia nervosa
  • D. Atypical anorexia nervosa
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: D

Atypical AN, an OSFED, meets all anorexia criteria except significantly low weight. Weight may be in or above the expected range, yet complications such as bradycardia and amenorrhea are present. BED has no restriction or compensation pattern. ARFID is avoidance without the fear of weight gain. BN requires binge eating with compensatory behaviors.

cards.prompt: A student nurse reviews feeding and eating disorders. Which statements are accurate? Select all that apply. A. Pica involves eating non-food substances for at least 1 month and can cause obstruction or poisoning. B. Rumination disorder involves repeated regurgitation with rechewing, reswallowing or spitting out. C. ARFID involves food avoidance from low interest, sensory issues or fear of consequences of eating. D. Purging disorder involves large binges followed by vomiting at least weekly. E. Night eating syndrome involves eating after waking from sleep or excessively after the evening meal.
cards.promptHtml:
A student nurse reviews feeding and eating disorders. Which statements are accurate? Select all that apply.

  • A. Pica involves eating non-food substances for at least 1 month and can cause obstruction or poisoning.
  • B. Rumination disorder involves repeated regurgitation with rechewing, reswallowing or spitting out.
  • C. ARFID involves food avoidance from low interest, sensory issues or fear of consequences of eating.
  • D. Purging disorder involves large binges followed by vomiting at least weekly.
  • E. Night eating syndrome involves eating after waking from sleep or excessively after the evening meal.
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: A, B, C, E

Options A, B, C and E match the lecture definitions. Purging disorder involves purging after normal amounts of food without binge eating, which distinguishes it from bulimia nervosa, so option D is false. Pica and rumination are not explained by another disorder, and ARFID is not driven by fear of weight gain.

cards.prompt: A patient with type 1 diabetes tells the nurse she has been skipping insulin doses to lose weight. Which assessment is the priority? A. Signs of diabetic ketoacidosis, including blood glucose, ketones and breathing pattern B. The patient's body mass index C. The patient's menstrual history D. The patient's family attitudes about weight
cards.promptHtml:
A patient with type 1 diabetes tells the nurse she has been skipping insulin doses to lose weight. Which assessment is the priority?

  • A. Signs of diabetic ketoacidosis, including blood glucose, ketones and breathing pattern
  • B. The patient's body mass index
  • C. The patient's menstrual history
  • D. The patient's family attitudes about weight
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: A

Deliberate insulin restriction for weight loss, called diabulimia in the lecture, can cause DKA, which is life-threatening. The nurse checks glucose, ketones, and respiratory and mental status first. BMI, menstrual history and family attitudes are important for the broader assessment but are not the immediate priority.

cards.prompt: A nurse cares for a patient with anorexia nervosa who says, "No one would even notice if I was gone." Which action is the priority? A. Ask the patient directly about thoughts of suicide and whether she has a plan B. Weigh the patient and record the result C. Provide a calorie count and explain the meal plan D. Document the statement and revisit it at the next therapy session
cards.promptHtml:
A nurse cares for a patient with anorexia nervosa who says, "No one would even notice if I was gone." Which action is the priority?

  • A. Ask the patient directly about thoughts of suicide and whether she has a plan
  • B. Weigh the patient and record the result
  • C. Provide a calorie count and explain the meal plan
  • D. Document the statement and revisit it at the next therapy session
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: A

Suicide and cardiopulmonary arrest are the leading causes of death in anorexia nervosa, and patients tend to use highly lethal means. Suicide risk is one of the two top priorities of care. The nurse asks directly and then follows policy for precautions. Routine weights and meal planning continue but come after safety. Delaying to the next session leaves the risk unaddressed.

cards.prompt: A school nurse meets a 15-year-old distance runner who skips meals, has not had a period in 5 months and has a stress fracture. The nurse recognizes this as which condition? A. Rumination disorder B. Female athlete triad C. Night eating syndrome D. Purging disorder
cards.promptHtml:
A school nurse meets a 15-year-old distance runner who skips meals, has not had a period in 5 months and has a stress fracture. The nurse recognizes this as which condition?

  • A. Rumination disorder
  • B. Female athlete triad
  • C. Night eating syndrome
  • D. Purging disorder
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: B

The female athlete triad is disordered eating, menstrual dysfunction and low bone density or osteoporosis. Athletes in lean sports such as running and gymnastics are at higher risk, and the stress fracture suggests bone loss. The other options do not fit: none involves the combination of restriction, amenorrhea and bone injury.

cards.prompt: Which nursing interventions are appropriate for an inpatient with anorexia nervosa who is in the early refeeding phase? Select all that apply. A. Record all food and fluid intake B. Weigh at the same time each day, after voiding, on the same scale C. Allow the patient to skip meals when anxiety is high to reduce conflict D. Monitor bathroom use, especially after meals E. Limit exercise and enforce rest
cards.promptHtml:
Which nursing interventions are appropriate for an inpatient with anorexia nervosa who is in the early refeeding phase? Select all that apply.

  • A. Record all food and fluid intake
  • B. Weigh at the same time each day, after voiding, on the same scale
  • C. Allow the patient to skip meals when anxiety is high to reduce conflict
  • D. Monitor bathroom use, especially after meals
  • E. Limit exercise and enforce rest
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: A, B, D, E

Accurate intake records and consistent weights guide the refeeding plan. Bathroom monitoring prevents hidden purging, and exercise is not permitted during refeeding because it burns needed calories. Skipping meals (C) reinforces restriction. If the patient cannot eat, the team provides calories another way, such as a liquid supplement or NG tube.

cards.prompt: A patient with bulimia nervosa says, "I eat almost nothing all day, then I lose control at night, make myself vomit and promise to be stricter tomorrow." Which teaching is most important for breaking this cycle? A. Weigh yourself every morning and again at night B. Keep a list of all the foods you must never eat C. Eat regular meals during the day so hunger and rigid rules do not trigger binges D. Exercise after every binge to make up for the calories
cards.promptHtml:
A patient with bulimia nervosa says, "I eat almost nothing all day, then I lose control at night, make myself vomit and promise to be stricter tomorrow." Which teaching is most important for breaking this cycle?

  • A. Weigh yourself every morning and again at night
  • B. Keep a list of all the foods you must never eat
  • C. Eat regular meals during the day so hunger and rigid rules do not trigger binges
  • D. Exercise after every binge to make up for the calories
cards.answerHtml:
Answer: C

Dietary restraint and strict food rules set up the next binge. Regular meals reduce hunger and rule-driven overeating, which also reduces purging. Frequent weighing keeps the focus on weight. Lists of forbidden foods reinforce rules. Exercise as compensation is a purging behavior in bulimia.
